title: Crop Master: Cotton
content: Crop: Cotton (ప్రత్తి (పత్తి), कपास). Scientific name: Gossypium hirsutum. Category: Commercial Fiber. Season: Kharif. Duration: 160 days. Soil: Deep black soils (Vertisols) or well-drained alluvial soils, pH 6.0 - 8.0. Water: 700 - 1200 mm.

title: Crop Master: Rice / Paddy
content: Crop: Rice / Paddy (వరి, धान / चावल). Scientific name: Oryza sativa. Category: Cereal Food Grain. Season: Kharif / Rabi. Duration: 125 days. Soil: Clayey loam, fertile alluvial soils with high water retention capacity, pH 5.5 - 7.0. Water: 1100 - 1500 mm.

title: Crop Master: Chilli
content: Crop: Chilli (మిరప, मिर्च). Scientific name: Capsicum annuum. Category: Spices / Cash Crop. Season: Kharif / Rabi. Duration: 150 days. Soil: Well-drained sandy loam or clay loam, rich in organic matter, pH 6.5 - 7.5. Water: 600 - 900 mm.

title: Crop Master: Tomato
content: Crop: Tomato (టమోటా, टमाटर). Scientific name: Solanum lycopersicum. Category: Vegetable. Season: Year-round. Duration: 110 days. Soil: Well-drained sandy loam with good moisture holding capacity, pH 6.0 - 7.0. Water: 400 - 600 mm.

title: Crop Master: Wheat
content: Crop: Wheat (గోధుమ, गेहूं). Scientific name: Triticum aestivum. Category: Cereal Food Grain. Season: Rabi. Duration: 120 days. Soil: Well-drained fertile loams and clay loams, rich in organic matter, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 450 - 650 mm.

title: Crop Master: Maize
content: Crop: Maize (మొక్కజొన్న, मक्का). Scientific name: Zea mays. Category: Cereal / Coarse Grain. Season: Kharif / Rabi / Spring. Duration: 105 days. Soil: Deep, well-drained sandy loam to silty clay loam with good organic matter, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 500 - 800 mm.

title: Crop Master: Groundnut / Peanut
content: Crop: Groundnut / Peanut (వేరుశనగ, मूंगफली). Scientific name: Arachis hypogaea. Category: Oilseed / Legume. Season: Kharif / Rabi / Summer. Duration: 115 days. Soil: Well-drained loose, friable red sandy loam or light alluvial soils, pH 6.0 - 7.0. Water: 500 - 700 mm.

title: Crop Master: Soybean
content: Crop: Soybean (సోయాబీన్, सोयाबीन). Scientific name: Glycine max. Category: Oilseed / Legume. Season: Kharif. Duration: 95 days. Soil: Well-drained fertile loamy to clayey black soils (Vertisols), pH 6.5 - 7.5. Water: 550 - 750 mm.

title: Crop Master: Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Crop: Red Gram / Pigeonpea (కందులు, अरहर / तुअर). Scientific name: Cajanus cajan. Category: Pulse / Legume. Season: Kharif. Duration: 165 days. Soil: Deep, well-drained loamy to heavy black cotton soils, pH 6.5 - 7.8. Water: 600 - 800 mm.

title: Crop Master: Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Crop: Chickpea / Bengal Gram (శనగలు, चना). Scientific name: Cicer arietinum. Category: Pulse / Legume. Season: Rabi. Duration: 105 days. Soil: Moderately heavy black soils (Vertisols) or light alluvial soils with good moisture retention, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 250 - 400 mm.

title: Crop Master: Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Crop: Mustard / Rapeseed (ఆవాలు, सरसों / राई). Scientific name: Brassica juncea. Category: Oilseed. Season: Rabi. Duration: 115 days. Soil: Light to heavy loam soils with fair moisture storage, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 300 - 450 mm.

title: Crop Master: Sugarcane
content: Crop: Sugarcane (చెరకు, गन्ना). Scientific name: Saccharum officinarum. Category: Commercial Cash Crop. Season: Annual / Adsali. Duration: 360 days. Soil: Deep well-drained fertile loamy to clay loam soils with high organic matter, pH 6.5 - 7.5. Water: 1500 - 2500 mm.

title: Crop Master: Onion
content: Crop: Onion (ఉల్లిపాయ, प्याज). Scientific name: Allium cepa. Category: Vegetable / Bulb. Season: Kharif / Late Kharif / Rabi. Duration: 130 days. Soil: Well-drained rich sandy loam to silty clay loam free from water stagnation, pH 6.0 - 7.0. Water: 350 - 550 mm.

title: Crop Master: Potato
content: Crop: Potato (బంగాళాదుంప (ఆలూ), आलू). Scientific name: Solanum tuberosum. Category: Vegetable / Tuber. Season: Rabi. Duration: 100 days. Soil: Friable, loose, well-aerated sandy loam rich in organic matter, pH 5.2 - 6.5. Water: 450 - 600 mm.

title: Crop Master: Turmeric
content: Crop: Turmeric (పసుపు, हल्दी). Scientific name: Curcuma longa. Category: Spices / Cash Crop. Season: Kharif. Duration: 240 days. Soil: Well-drained loose, friable red loamy or clay loam rich in humus, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 1200 - 1800 mm.

title: Crop Master: Black Gram / Urad
content: Crop: Black Gram / Urad (మినుములు, उड़द). Scientific name: Vigna mungo. Category: Pulse / Legume. Season: Kharif / Rabi / Summer. Duration: 75 days. Soil: Well-drained fertile loam to clay loam, pH 6.0 - 7.5. Water: 350 - 500 mm.

title: Cultivation Guide: Cotton
content: Agronomy for Cotton: Seed rate: 1.8 - 2.2 kg (Bt hybrid seeds - 2 packets of 450g each). Spacing: 90 cm x 60 cm (Normal black soil) or 120 cm x 45 cm (High density). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 15 to July 15 (After receiving 50-60 mm monsoon rainfall)'}. Land preparation: Deep ploughing with mould-board plough once in 3 years followed by 2-3 harrowings. Incorporate 5 tonnes well-decomposed FYM per acre.. Sowing method: Dibbling 1 seed per hill at 3-4 cm depth with non-Bt refuge border rows.. Plant population: 7,400 hills/acre (at 90x60 cm).

title: Cultivation Guide: Rice / Paddy
content: Agronomy for Rice / Paddy: Seed rate: 20 - 25 kg (Fine varieties) / 25 - 30 kg (Coarse varieties) for transplanted; 12 - 15 kg for drum seeding / DSR. Spacing: 15 cm x 15 cm or 20 cm x 15 cm (Transplanted). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'Nursery: May 25 to June 20; Transplanting: June 25 to July 20', 'rabi': 'Nursery: Nov 15 to Dec 10; Transplanting: Dec 15 to Jan 10'}. Land preparation: Puddle 2-3 times in standing water followed by leveling using wooden leveller. Keep 2-3 cm standing water.. Sowing method: Wet bed nursery (400 sq.m per acre). Transplant 25-30 day old seedlings @ 2-3 seedlings per hill.. Plant population: 133,000 to 177,000 hills/acre.
citation: PJTSAU Rice Agronomy Manual 2025 & ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad

title: Cultivation Guide: Chilli
content: Agronomy for Chilli: Seed rate: 200 - 250 g (Hybrids) / 400 - 500 g (Varieties). Spacing: 60 cm x 60 cm or 75 cm x 45 cm (Hybrids). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'Nursery: June-July; Transplanting: July-August', 'rabi': 'Nursery: September-October; Transplanting: October-November'}. Land preparation: 3-4 deep ploughings and planking to bring soil to fine tilth. Form ridges and furrows at 60 cm distance. Apply 8-10 tonnes FYM/acre.. Sowing method: Pro-tray nursery with cocopeat or raised nursery beds. Transplant 35-40 day old healthy seedlings.. Plant population: 11,000 to 14,000 plants/acre.
citation: PJTSAU Chilli Package of Practices 2025 & ICAR-IIHR Bengaluru

title: Cultivation Guide: Tomato
content: Agronomy for Tomato: Seed rate: 60 - 80 g (Hybrids) / 150 - 200 g (Open Pollinated). Spacing: 90 cm x 45 cm or 120 cm x 60 cm (Staked hybrids). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June to July', 'rabi': 'October to November', 'zaid_summer': 'January to February'}. Land preparation: Plough field 4 times to fine tilth, make broad beds of 90 cm width with 30 cm furrow or ridges at 90 cm.. Sowing method: Pro-tray seedling raising using 98-celled trays. Transplant 25-30 day seedlings in afternoon.. Plant population: 7,400 to 9,800 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Wheat
content: Agronomy for Wheat: Seed rate: 40 - 45 kg (Timely sown) / 50 - 55 kg (Late sown). Spacing: 20 - 22.5 cm row spacing (Continuous seed drill sowing). Sowing windows: {'rabi_timely': 'November 1 to November 20 (Optimal)', 'rabi_late': 'November 21 to December 10'}. Land preparation: 1 ploughing with disc plough followed by 2 cross harrowings and planking to make a weed-free, firm seedbed.. Sowing method: Seed drill or Zero-till ferti-seed drill at depth of 4-5 cm into adequate residual moisture.. Plant population: Approximately 180,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Maize
content: Agronomy for Maize: Seed rate: 7 - 8 kg (Single cross hybrids) / 10 kg (Composite varieties). Spacing: 60 cm x 20 cm (Normal) or 75 cm x 20 cm (Winter maize). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 15 to July 15', 'rabi': 'October 15 to November 15'}. Land preparation: Plough to 15-20 cm depth, harrowing twice, leveling. Open ridges and furrows at 60 cm spacing.. Sowing method: Direct dibbling at 4-5 cm depth on ridge slopes (1/3rd from bottom).. Plant population: 26,000 to 33,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Groundnut / Peanut
content: Agronomy for Groundnut / Peanut: Seed rate: 40 - 45 kg kernels (Bunch types) / 35 - 40 kg (Spreading types). Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm (Bunch types) or 30 cm x 15 cm. Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 15 to July 15', 'rabi_summer': 'October 15 to November 15 (Rabi) / January 1 to January 20 (Summer)'}. Land preparation: Plough field 2-3 times to create friable, loose topsoil to allow easy peg penetration.. Sowing method: Seed drill or manual dibbling at 5 cm depth. Treat seed with Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg seed + Rhizobium @ 250g/10kg.. Plant population: 133,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Soybean
content: Agronomy for Soybean: Seed rate: 25 - 30 kg (Seed germination must be >70%). Spacing: 45 cm x 5 cm or 30 cm x 7.5 cm (Broad bed furrow BBF method recommended). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 20 to July 10 (Sow after 75-100 mm accumulated monsoon rainfall)'}. Land preparation: Deep summer ploughing once in 3 years. 2 harrowings and planking. BBF machine forms 45 cm beds with furrows.. Sowing method: Direct drilling at 3-4 cm depth. Inoculate with Bradyrhizobium japonicum @ 5g/kg seed.. Plant population: 177,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Agronomy for Red Gram / Pigeonpea: Seed rate: 4 - 5 kg (Medium duration sole crop) / 2 kg (Intercrop with Cotton 4:1). Spacing: 120 cm x 20 cm or 150 cm x 30 cm (Sole crop in black soil). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 15 to July 15 (Avoid sowing beyond July 31)'}. Land preparation: Plough deep to break hardpan. Red soils require 2-3 passes of cultivator and leveling.. Sowing method: Direct drilling or dibbling 2 seeds per hill at 4-5 cm depth. Thin to 1 seedling at 15 DAS.. Plant population: 13,300 to 16,600 plants/acre.
citation: PJTSAU Pulses Vyavasaya Panchangam & ICAR-IIPR Kanpur

title: Cultivation Guide: Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Agronomy for Chickpea / Bengal Gram: Seed rate: 25 - 30 kg (Desi varieties) / 40 - 45 kg (Kabuli varieties). Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm. Sowing windows: {'rabi': 'October 15 to November 15 (Sow when maximum daily temp drops below 30°C)'}. Land preparation: Rough seedbed is preferred over fine pulverization to preserve black soil moisture and reduce root rot.. Sowing method: Direct drilling at 5-7 cm depth into moist subsoil. Seed treatment with Mesorhizobium ciceri.. Plant population: 133,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Agronomy for Mustard / Rapeseed: Seed rate: 1.5 - 2.0 kg. Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm (Timely) / 45 cm x 15 cm (High vigor hybrids). Sowing windows: {'rabi': 'October 1 to October 25 (Crucial to escape aphid infestation in January)'}. Land preparation: Firm, moist, weed-free seedbed. 2-3 harrowings followed by light planking to retain soil moisture.. Sowing method: Direct drilling at shallow depth of 3-4 cm. Thinning at 15-20 DAS is mandatory to maintain 1 plant/hill.. Plant population: 88,000 to 133,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Sugarcane
content: Agronomy for Sugarcane: Seed rate: 25,000 two-budded setts or 16,000 three-budded setts per acre (Approx 3 - 3.5 tonnes cane). Spacing: 120 cm or 150 cm wide-row trench / furrow spacing. Sowing windows: {'spring_planting': 'February to March', 'autumn_planting': 'October to November', 'adsali_planting': 'July to August (Maharashtra/Telangana)'}. Land preparation: Deep chiseling up to 45 cm followed by disc harrowing. Open deep furrows/trenches 30 cm deep.. Sowing method: End-to-end sett planting in furrows. Dip setts in Carbendazim 0.1% solution for 15 minutes before placing.. Plant population: 35,000 to 45,000 millable canes/acre target.

title: Cultivation Guide: Onion
content: Agronomy for Onion: Seed rate: 3 - 4 kg (Nursery raising for transplanting). Spacing: 15 cm x 10 cm (Flat beds or broad beds). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'Nursery: May-June; Transplanting: July-August', 'late_kharif_rangada': 'Nursery: August-September; Transplanting: September-October', 'rabi': 'Nursery: October-November; Transplanting: December-January'}. Land preparation: Plough 3 times to bring soil to friable condition. Prepare flat beds (3m x 2m) or broad bed furrows (120 cm top, 30 cm furrow).. Sowing method: Transplant 6-7 week old seedlings (15 cm tall with pencil thickness). Clip top 1/3rd leaf before planting.. Plant population: 260,000 plants/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Potato
content: Agronomy for Potato: Seed rate: 10 - 12 quintals (Tubers of 30-40g size with 2-3 active sprouted eyes). Spacing: 60 cm x 20 cm. Sowing windows: {'rabi': 'October 15 to November 10'}. Land preparation: Deep ploughing 20-25 cm, 2 rotavator runs to produce soft clod-free soil. Ridges formed at 60 cm distance.. Sowing method: Plant well-chitted tubers 5-7 cm deep on ridges and cover with 5-7 cm soil. Earth-up at 30 DAS.. Plant population: 33,000 hills/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Turmeric
content: Agronomy for Turmeric: Seed rate: 8 - 10 quintals (Healthy mother rhizomes or primary fingers with 2 buds). Spacing: 45 cm x 20 cm on ridges or 30 cm x 20 cm on raised beds (120 cm width). Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'May 15 to June 30'}. Land preparation: Plough 4-5 times, incorporate 10 tonnes FYM/acre + 200 kg neem cake. Form raised beds or ridges.. Sowing method: Plant finger rhizomes 4-5 cm deep. Apply green leaf mulch @ 5 tonnes/acre immediately after planting.. Plant population: 44,000 to 66,000 hills/acre.

title: Cultivation Guide: Black Gram / Urad
content: Agronomy for Black Gram / Urad: Seed rate: 6 - 8 kg (Kharif) / 8 - 10 kg (Rabi / Rice fallow). Spacing: 30 cm x 10 cm. Sowing windows: {'kharif': 'June 15 to July 15', 'rabi_rice_fallow': 'November 15 to December 15 (Broadcast into standing paddy 2-3 days before harvest)'}. Land preparation: 1-2 ploughings and harrowing. For rice-fallow, no land prep is required (relay dibbling).. Sowing method: Seed drill or line sowing. Treat with Rhizobium and PSB culture @ 20g/kg seed.. Plant population: 133,000 plants/acre.

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Cotton
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Cotton: 00-09 (Germination & Emergence 1 - 7 DAS): Radicle emergence and cotyledon unfolding above soil.; 10-19 (Leaf Development 8 - 30 DAS): 1st to 8th true leaves unfolded on main stem.; 20-29 (Monopodial Branching 30 - 45 DAS): Vegetative branches emerge from lower nodes.; 50-59 (Squaring (Floral Bud Formation) 45 - 65 DAS): Appearance of triangular flower squares on sympodial branches.; 60-69 (Flowering & Anthesis 65 - 90 DAS): White/cream flowers open, turn pink-red on day 2 after pollination.; 70-79 (Boll Development 90 - 130 DAS): Green bolls enlarge rapidly and reach final physiological size.; 80-89 (Boll Bursting & Maturity 130 - 160 DAS): Capsule valves split, locules flare open, exposing dry white lint.; 90-99 (Senescence & Stalk Clearance 160 - 180 DAS): Leaves senesce; terminal picking completed; crop stalks shredded..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Rice / Paddy
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Rice / Paddy: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 5 DAS): Coleoptile penetrates husk; radicle elongates.; 10-19 (Seedling / Leaf Stage 6 - 25 DAS): Seedlings develop 3-4 leaves in nursery bed before transplanting.; 20-29 (Tillering Stage 25 - 50 DAT): Primary and secondary tillers emerge; maximum tillering reached.; 30-39 (Stem Elongation / Panicle Initiation 50 - 65 DAT): Internode elongation begins; green ring visible at growing point.; 40-49 (Booting Stage 65 - 75 DAT): Flag leaf sheath swells significantly enclosing developing panicle.; 50-59 (Panicle Heading 75 - 85 DAT): Panicle emerges 50% to 100% from flag leaf sheath.; 60-69 (Flowering / Anthesis 85 - 92 DAT): Spikelets open between 9 AM and 1 PM; self-pollination occurs.; 70-79 (Milking Stage 92 - 105 DAT): Caryopsis filled with white milky starch; spikelets turn light green.; 80-89 (Dough & Maturation Stage 105 - 120 DAT): Soft dough hardens into firm grain; panicles turn golden yellow.; 90-99 (Full Ripening & Harvest 120 - 130 DAT): Grain moisture drops below 20%; ready for combine or manual harvest..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Chilli
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Chilli: 00-09 (Germination & Seedling 1 - 35 DAS): Nursery development of true leaves up to 5-6 leaf stage.; 20-29 (Vegetative Branching 15 - 40 DAT): Dichotomous branching from main stem into bushy canopy.; 50-59 (Flower Bud Initiation 40 - 55 DAT): Solitary star-shaped buds form at branch axils.; 60-69 (Flowering & Fruit Set 55 - 75 DAT): White petals open; ovary swells into elongated green berry.; 70-79 (Fruit Development & Green Picking 75 - 105 DAT): Pod reaches full length and firmness; green chilli harvest starts.; 80-89 (Red Ripening & Drying 105 - 150 DAT): Fruits transition from dark green to deep crimson red; multiple pickings..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Tomato
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Tomato: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 25 DAS): Pro-tray nursery emergence and development to 4 true leaves.; 20-29 (Vegetative & Side Shoots 10 - 30 DAT): Bush expansion; side suckers pruned in indeterminate types.; 50-59 (Inflorescence Emergence 30 - 45 DAT): First flower clusters (trusses) appear on main stem.; 60-69 (Flowering & Anthesis 45 - 60 DAT): Yellow flowers open; corolla reflexed; self-fertilization.; 70-79 (Fruit Growth (Green Stage) 60 - 80 DAT): Berries enlarge from pea size to mature green stage.; 80-89 (Breaker to Red Ripe Stage 80 - 110 DAT): Breaker, turning, pink, light red to firm red ripe stages; multiple harvests..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Wheat
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Wheat: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 7 DAS): Coleoptile penetrates surface; 1st leaf emerges.; 10-19 (Crown Root Initiation (CRI) 20 - 25 DAS): Crown roots initiate at 2 cm below soil; most critical irrigation stage.; 20-29 (Tillering Stage 25 - 45 DAS): Tillers branch from crown nodes; tillering capacity defined.; 30-39 (Jointing / Stem Elongation 45 - 65 DAS): Nodes rise above ground; stem elongates rapidly.; 40-49 (Booting Stage 65 - 75 DAS): Flag leaf sheath bulges with spike enclosed.; 50-59 (Heading / Ear Emergence 75 - 85 DAS): Spike completely emerges from flag leaf collar.; 60-69 (Anthesis / Flowering 85 - 92 DAS): Anthers extrude from florets; pollination complete.; 70-79 (Milk Stage 92 - 105 DAS): Grain content watery to milky white.; 80-89 (Dough & Hard Maturity 105 - 120 DAS): Grain passes soft to hard dough; straw turns bright golden yellow..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Maize
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Maize: 00-09 (Emergence (VE) 1 - 6 DAS): Coleoptile pierces soil surface.; 10-19 (Knee-High Stage (V6-V8) 25 - 35 DAS): Rapid stem elongation; tassel begins forming deep in stem.; 50-59 (Tasseling (VT) 50 - 60 DAS): Male inflorescence (tassel) emerges completely at top of plant.; 60-69 (Silking (R1) 55 - 65 DAS): Female silks emerge from ear tip; pollen shed from tassel.; 70-79 (Blister & Milk Stage (R2-R3) 65 - 80 DAS): Kernels resemble blisters filled with clear then milky fluid.; 80-89 (Dent & Physiological Maturity (R5-R6) 80 - 105 DAS): Black layer forms at base of kernel; husk leaves dry out completely..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Groundnut / Peanut
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Groundnut / Peanut: 00-09 (Germination & Emergence 1 - 8 DAS): Hypocotyl pushes cotyledons; 4-tetrafoliate leaves unfold.; 20-29 (Vegetative Branching 15 - 30 DAS): Lateral branches develop from main axis.; 50-59 (Flowering Initiation 25 - 35 DAS): Yellow flowers appear at lower nodes in morning.; 60-69 (Pegging (Gynophore Elongation) 35 - 50 DAS): Peg turns downwards, penetrates soil 3-5 cm.; 70-79 (Pod Development 50 - 85 DAS): Peg tip swells horizontally underground into shell and kernel.; 80-89 (Pod Maturity 85 - 115 DAS): Inner pod shell develops dark brownish-black vascular netting..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Soybean
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Soybean: 00-09 (Emergence (VE-VC) 1 - 6 DAS): Cotyledons emerge and unifoliate leaves unfold.; 10-19 (Trifoliate Development (V1-V4) 7 - 25 DAS): 1st to 4th trifoliate leaves fully developed on main stem.; 50-59 (First Flower (R1-R2) 30 - 45 DAS): One open flower at any node; full bloom across canopy.; 70-79 (Pod & Seed Development (R3-R5) 45 - 75 DAS): Pods 5 mm to 2 cm long; beans fill cavity completely.; 80-89 (Maturity & Leaf Drop (R7-R8) 75 - 95 DAS): Pods turn tan/brown; 95% leaves senesce and drop; pods rattle..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Red Gram / Pigeonpea: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 8 DAS): Epigeal germination; two cotyledonary leaves emerge.; 20-29 (Vegetative Branching 20 - 70 DAS): Profuse primary and secondary branching; deep taproot growth.; 50-59 (Flower Bud Formation 70 - 100 DAS): Terminal and axillary racemes bear bright yellow flower buds.; 60-69 (Pod Setting 100 - 125 DAS): Ovaries develop into green glandular pubescent pods.; 80-89 (Pod Ripening & Maturity 125 - 165 DAS): Pods turn dark brown; seeds harden; ready for harvesting..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Chickpea / Bengal Gram: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 7 DAS): Hypogeal germination; plumule emerges above ground.; 20-29 (Vegetative Branching & Nipping 15 - 40 DAS): Primary and secondary branches; terminal nipping at 30-35 DAS.; 50-59 (Flowering Initiation 40 - 60 DAS): Pink/purple or white flowers emerge from leaf axils.; 70-79 (Pod Development 60 - 85 DAS): Inflated pods develop enclosing 1-2 green seeds.; 80-89 (Maturity & Drying 85 - 105 DAS): Foliage and pods turn straw-yellow; seeds shake inside pods..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Mustard / Rapeseed
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Mustard / Rapeseed: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 5 DAS): Cotyledons emerge and expand into heart shape.; 20-29 (Rosette Stage 15 - 35 DAS): Lower leaves form dense horizontal rosette.; 30-39 (Bolting / Stem Elongation 35 - 50 DAS): Central flower stalk shoots upward rapidly.; 60-69 (Flowering Stage 50 - 75 DAS): Bright yellow 4-petaled flowers bloom continuously.; 70-79 (Siliqua (Pod) Formation 75 - 95 DAS): Long beaked siliquae develop filled with green round seeds.; 80-89 (Ripening Stage 95 - 115 DAS): Pods turn yellowish-brown; seeds turn dark reddish-brown/black..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Sugarcane
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Sugarcane: 00-09 (Germination / Sprouting 1 - 35 DAP): Buds on setts sprout and roots establish.; 20-29 (Tillering (Formative Stage) 35 - 120 DAP): Underground nodal buds produce tillers; canopy closure.; 30-39 (Grand Growth Stage 120 - 270 DAP): Rapid cane elongation; internode formation; high water/nutrient demand.; 80-89 (Ripening & Sugar Accumulation 270 - 360 DAP): Vegetative growth slows; sucrose accumulates in stalk tissue..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Onion
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Onion: 00-09 (Germination & Seedling 1 - 45 DAS): Nursery loop stage; cotyledon straightens; 3-4 leaves develop.; 10-19 (Vegetative Leaf Growth 15 - 60 DAT): Hollow tubular leaves emerge alternately from growing point.; 40-49 (Bulb Initiation & Swelling 60 - 100 DAT): Leaf sheaths swell at base; bulb diameter expands rapidly.; 80-89 (Neck Fall & Maturity 100 - 130 DAT): 50-70% pseudo-stems soften and tops collapse ('neck fall')..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Potato
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Potato: 00-09 (Sprouting & Emergence 1 - 15 DAP): Eyes sprout underground; stems and compound leaves emerge.; 20-29 (Stolon Formation 15 - 30 DAP): Underground horizontal stems (stolons) branch from basal nodes.; 40-49 (Tuber Initiation 30 - 45 DAP): Stolon tips swell into marble-sized tuberlets.; 70-79 (Tuber Bulking 45 - 80 DAP): Rapid deposition of starch; tuber size doubles every 10-14 days.; 80-89 (Skin Curing & Maturity 80 - 100 DAP): Haulms senesce or dehaulmed; tuber skin thickens and sets..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Turmeric
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Turmeric: 00-09 (Rhizome Sprouting 1 - 25 DAP): Mother rhizome buds swell and shoot emerges through mulch.; 10-19 (Tillering & Leaf Development 25 - 90 DAP): Large broad oblong lanceolate leaves produce pseudostem tillers.; 40-49 (Rhizome Initiation & Bulking 90 - 180 DAP): Primary and secondary finger rhizomes grow vigorously underground.; 80-89 (Maturity & Foliage Drying 180 - 240 DAP): Leaves turn yellow and dry down completely; rhizomes ready for harvest..

title: BBCH Growth Stages: Black Gram / Urad
content: BBCH Growth Stages for Black Gram / Urad: 00-09 (Germination 1 - 5 DAS): Hypogeal germination; seedling emerges with first unifoliate leaves.; 20-29 (Vegetative Branching 10 - 25 DAS): Trifoliate leaves form with short lateral branches.; 50-59 (Flowering 25 - 40 DAS): Self-fertile pale yellow flowers cluster at branch tips.; 70-79 (Pod Filling 40 - 60 DAS): Slender cylindrical hairy pods develop enclosing 6-10 seeds.; 80-89 (Maturity & Blackening 60 - 75 DAS): Pods turn completely black; single or two-stage harvest..

title: Disease: Rice Blast in Rice / Paddy
content: Disease: Rice Blast (వరి అగ్గితెగులు, धान का झुलसा रोग) in Rice / Paddy. Pathogen: Fungal (Magnaporthe oryzae / Pyricularia oryzae). Symptoms: Spindle-shaped / diamond-shaped lesions on leaves with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers. Neck blast causes blackening of neck node, panicles break and hang down, producing empty chaffy grains.. Favorable weather: High relative humidity (>90%), night temperature 19-23°C, prolonged morning dew (4-6 hours), overcast skies..

title: Disease: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot in Cotton
content: Disease: Bacterial Blight / Angular Leaf Spot (బాక్టీరియా ఆకుమచ్చ తెగులు, जीवाणु झुलसा रोग) in Cotton. Pathogen: Bacterial (Xanthomonas citri pv. malvacearum). Symptoms: Small, water-soaked, angular spots on leaves delimited by veins. Lesions coalesce turning reddish-brown to black. Progresses along veins to petioles and stems causing 'black arm', and rotting of young bolls.. Favorable weather: Warm temperature (28-32°C), high humidity (>85%), wind-driven rain showers..

title: Disease: Early Blight in Tomato
content: Disease: Early Blight (ముందస్తు తెగులు (ఆకుమచ్చ), अगेती झुलसा) in Tomato. Pathogen: Fungal (Alternaria solani). Symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with characteristic concentric rings ('target board' appearance) on lower leaves first. Stem lesions cause collar rot. Sunken leathery dark lesions develop at stem end of fruits.. Favorable weather: Warm temperature (24-29°C), alternating wet and dry periods, heavy dew..

title: Disease: Sheath Blight in Rice / Paddy
content: Disease: Sheath Blight (వరి పాము పొడ తెగులు, शीथ ब्लाइट / पर्णच्छद झुलसा) in Rice / Paddy. Pathogen: Fungal (Rhizoctonia solani). Symptoms: Oval or elliptical greenish-grey water-soaked spots on leaf sheaths near waterline. Lesions enlarge and coalesce with irregular snake-skin pattern bordered by dark brown bands. Spreads upward to flag leaves.. Favorable weather: High relative humidity (85-100%), temperature 28-32°C, dense plant canopy, excessive nitrogen fertilizer..

title: Disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) in Rice / Paddy
content: Disease: Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB) (బాక్టీరియా ఎండు తెగులు, जीवाणु पत्ती झुलसा) in Rice / Paddy. Pathogen: Bacterial (Xanthomonas oryzae pv. oryzae). Symptoms: Water-soaked streaks starting at leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy yellowish-white lesions that turn greyish-white. Milky bacterial ooze droplets appear on young lesions in morning. 'Kresek' phase causes seedling wilting.. Favorable weather: Temperature 25-34°C, relative humidity >70%, strong winds with continuous rains..

title: Disease: Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease in Cotton
content: Disease: Grey Mildew / Dahiya Disease (దూది తెగులు (బూడిద తెగులు), दहिया रोग / धूसर फफूंदी) in Cotton. Pathogen: Fungal (Ramularia areola). Symptoms: Angular, pale translucent spots on lower surface of leaves covered with white powdery frosty growth resembling dusting of wheat flour (dahiya). Leaves turn yellowish brown, curl, dry and drop prematurely.. Favorable weather: Cool night temperatures (20-22°C), high humidity (>80%), cloudy weather in October-November..

title: Disease: Root Rot & Wilt Complex in Cotton
content: Disease: Root Rot & Wilt Complex (వేరుకుళ్లు మరియు ఎండు తెగులు, जड़ सड़न एवं उकठा रोग) in Cotton. Pathogen: Fungal (Rhizoctonia bataticola & Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. vasinfectum). Symptoms: Sudden wilting of standing plants in patches. Taproot shows shredding of bark, dark brown vascular discoloration, and shedding of lateral fibrous roots. Plants pull out easily from soil.. Favorable weather: High soil temperatures (35-39°C), low soil moisture followed by sudden heavy irrigation, alkaline soils..

title: Disease: Anthracnose / Fruit Rot / Die-Back in Chilli
content: Disease: Anthracnose / Fruit Rot / Die-Back (కొమ్మ ఎండు తెగులు మరియు కాయ కుళ్లు, फल सड़न एवं डाई-बैक) in Chilli. Pathogen: Fungal (Colletotrichum capsici). Symptoms: Circular sunken spots on ripe red fruits with black concentric rings containing fungal acervuli. Die-back begins as tender twig tips dry backwards from top to bottom, turning dirty white with black dots.. Favorable weather: Temperature 28-30°C, relative humidity >80%, intermittent rain showers after fruit setting..

title: Disease: Powdery Mildew in Chilli
content: Disease: Powdery Mildew (బూడిద తెగులు, चूर्णिल आसिता) in Chilli. Pathogen: Fungal (Leveillula taurica). Symptoms: White powdery fungal patches on the lower surface of mature leaves. Upper leaf surface displays corresponding chlorotic yellow patches. Causes severe defoliation leaving bare twigs.. Favorable weather: Warm dry days (25-30°C) with cool humid nights (60-70% RH) in December-February..

title: Disease: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus in Chilli
content: Disease: Chilli Leaf Curl Virus (బొబ్బర తెగులు (ఆకుముడుత), पत्ती मरोड़ विषाणु (लीफ कर्ल)) in Chilli. Pathogen: Viral (Chilli leaf curl virus - Begomovirus transmitted by Whitefly Bemisia tabaci). Symptoms: Upward curling and puckering of leaves, thickening of veins, shortened internodes resulting in extreme plant stunting (witches' broom effect). Drastic reduction in flowering and fruit size.. Favorable weather: Dry, hot weather favoring explosive population growth of whitefly vectors..

title: Disease: Late Blight in Tomato
content: Disease: Late Blight (ఆలస్యపు తెగులు (లేట్ బ్లైట్), पछेती झुलसा) in Tomato. Pathogen: Oomycete / Fungal-like (Phytophthora infestans). Symptoms: Water-soaked irregular blackish-brown lesions on leaves and stems. Under humid conditions, white delicate fungal downy growth appears on underside of leaves. Fruits show large, firm, greasy brown sunken blotches.. Favorable weather: Cool temperatures (12-18°C), high relative humidity (>90%), continuous drizzle or persistent fog..

title: Disease: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) in Tomato
content: Disease: Tomato Leaf Curl Virus (ToLCV) (టమోటా ఆకుముడుత వైరస్ తెగులు, टमाटर लीफ कर्ल वायरस) in Tomato. Pathogen: Viral (Tomato leaf curl virus - Begomovirus vectored by Whitefly). Symptoms: Severe upward and inward leaf curling, interveinal chlorosis, marked reduction in leaf size, bushy stunted appearance. Flowers drop prematurely; no marketable fruit set.. Favorable weather: High temperatures (30-35°C) and low rainfall which favor heavy whitefly breeding..

title: Disease: Yellow / Stripe Rust in Wheat
content: Disease: Yellow / Stripe Rust (పసుపు కుంకుమ తెగులు, पीला रतुआ / धारीदार गेरुआ) in Wheat. Pathogen: Fungal (Puccinia striiformis f. sp. tritici). Symptoms: Bright yellow pustules (uredinia) arranged in narrow, parallel linear stripes along leaf veins. Upon rubbing, yellow powder adheres to fingers. Chlorosis and leaf drying follow rapidly.. Favorable weather: Cool humid weather (temperature 10-15°C), intermittent rains, morning dew in North-Western plain zone..
citation: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal Yellow Rust Surveillance Protocol 2025

title: Disease: Brown / Leaf Rust in Wheat
content: Disease: Brown / Leaf Rust (గోధుమ కుంకుమ తెగులు, भूरा रतुआ) in Wheat. Pathogen: Fungal (Puccinia triticina). Symptoms: Small, round to oval, orange-brown pustules scattered randomly across leaf blades (not in stripes). Later turn black (telia) as plant approaches maturity.. Favorable weather: Moderate temperature (20-25°C) and high humidity with dew in Central and Peninsular zones..

title: Disease: Karnal Bunt in Wheat
content: Disease: Karnal Bunt (కర్నాల్ బంట్, करनाल बंट) in Wheat. Pathogen: Fungal (Tilletia indica). Symptoms: Only a few grains in the earhead are partially converted into black powdery teliospore mass. Diseased grains emit foul fishy odor due to trimethylamine gas.. Favorable weather: Cool cloudy weather, high humidity, light showers during wheat flowering stage (anthesis)..

title: Disease: Turcicum Leaf Blight (TLB) in Maize
content: Disease: Turcicum Leaf Blight (TLB) (మొక్కజొన్న ఆకు ఎండు తెగులు, टर्सिकम पर्ण झुलसा) in Maize. Pathogen: Fungal (Exserohilum turcicum / Helminthosporium turcicum). Symptoms: Long, elliptical, spindle-shaped greyish-green to tan lesions (2.5 - 15 cm long) on leaves. Lesions merge causing extensive leaf blighting. Appears first on lower leaves and progresses upward.. Favorable weather: Moderate temperatures (18-27°C), heavy dews, relative humidity >80%..

title: Disease: Maydis Leaf Blight (MLB) in Maize
content: Disease: Maydis Leaf Blight (MLB) (మేడిస్ ఆకుమచ్చ తెగులు, मेयडिस पर्ण झुलसा) in Maize. Pathogen: Fungal (Bipolaris maydis). Symptoms: Small, rectangular to oval tan spots with buff to reddish-brown borders strictly confined between leaf veins. Spots coalesce causing premature foliage death.. Favorable weather: Warm temperature (20-30°C) with high relative humidity (>85%)..

title: Disease: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late Leaf Spot) in Groundnut / Peanut
content: Disease: Tikka Leaf Spot (Early & Late Leaf Spot) (టిక్కా ఆకుమచ్చ తెగులు, टिक्का रोग / पर्ण चित्ती) in Groundnut / Peanut. Pathogen: Fungal (Cercospora arachidicola & Phaeoisariopsis personata). Symptoms: Early spot: Circular brown lesions surrounded by prominent yellow halo. Late spot: Dark carbon-black circular spots without prominent yellow halo on lower leaf surface. Severe premature defoliation leaves naked stems.. Favorable weather: Prolonged leaf wetness, temperature 25-30°C, RH >80% for 3-4 consecutive days..

title: Disease: Collar Rot / Crown Rot in Groundnut / Peanut
content: Disease: Collar Rot / Crown Rot (మొలక కుళ్లు / మెడ కుళ్లు తెగులు, कॉलर सड़न) in Groundnut / Peanut. Pathogen: Fungal (Aspergillus niger). Symptoms: Emerging seedlings collapse and rot at soil line. Collar region covered with profuse black sooty masses of fungal spores. Taproot decays completely.. Favorable weather: Deep sowing, high soil temperature (30-35°C), low soil moisture at seedling stage..

title: Disease: Soybean Rust in Soybean
content: Disease: Soybean Rust (సోయాబీన్ తుప్పు తెగులు, सोयाबीन गेरुआ रोग) in Soybean. Pathogen: Fungal (Phakopsora pachyrhizi). Symptoms: Pinhead-sized grey to tan polygonal pustules (uredinia) on underside of leaves. Pustules erupt releasing brown spores; foliage yellows, desiccates and sheds prematurely.. Favorable weather: Moderate temperature (18-26°C), continuous wet weather (>6 hours dew), RH >80%..

title: Disease: Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) in Soybean
content: Disease: Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) (పసుపు పచ్చ వైరస్ తెగులు, पीला मोज़ेक वायरस) in Soybean. Pathogen: Viral (Mungbean yellow mosaic India virus vectored by Whitefly). Symptoms: Alternating bright yellow and dark green mosaic patches on young trifoliate leaves. Leaves become leathery, puckered; pods remain small with shriveled seeds.. Favorable weather: Dry periods during monsoon promoting rapid whitefly multiplication..

title: Disease: Fusarium Wilt in Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Disease: Fusarium Wilt (కంది ఎండు తెగులు, अरहर उकठा रोग) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea. Pathogen: Fungal (Fusarium udum). Symptoms: Loss of turgidity, wilting and drooping of leaves starting on one side of plant. Splitting the main stem reveals a prominent dark purple-black vascular streak under the bark.. Favorable weather: Soil temperature 20-25°C, continuous cropping of pigeonpea in Vertisols..

title: Disease: Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Disease: Sterility Mosaic Disease (SMD) (గొడ్రాలితనం తెగులు (స్టెరిలిటీ మొజాయిక్), बांझपन मोज़ेक रोग) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea. Pathogen: Viral (Pigeonpea sterility mosaic virus vectored by Eriophyid mite Aceria cajani). Symptoms: Bushy stunted growth, mosaic mottling of leaves, total cessation of floral bud formation (sterility). Affected plants stand out green without bearing pods.. Favorable weather: High humidity and warm conditions favoring eriophyid mite populations..

title: Disease: Fusarium Wilt in Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Disease: Fusarium Wilt (శనగ ఎండు తెగులు, चना उकठा रोग) in Chickpea / Bengal Gram. Pathogen: Fungal (Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. ciceris). Symptoms: Sudden drooping and drying of petiole and pinnae without prior yellowing. Internal vascular tissues turn dark brown to black when taproot is split vertically.. Favorable weather: Warm soil temperatures (above 25°C) at seedling and pod-filling stages, dry soil conditions..

title: Disease: White Rust in Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Disease: White Rust (తెల్ల తుప్పు తెగులు, सफेद रतुआ) in Mustard / Rapeseed. Pathogen: Oomycete / Fungal-like (Albugo candida). Symptoms: White or creamy porcelain-like pustules (blisters) on underside of leaves. Systemic floral infection causes hypertrophied floral malformation known as 'staghead'.. Favorable weather: Cool moist weather (temperature 12-16°C), morning fog and RH >80%..

title: Disease: Alternaria Blight in Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Disease: Alternaria Blight (ఆల్టర్నేరియా ఆకుమచ్చ తెగులు, अल्टरनेरिया झुलसा) in Mustard / Rapeseed. Pathogen: Fungal (Alternaria brassicae & Alternaria brassicicola). Symptoms: Concentric circular target-board spots on leaves, stems and pods (siliquae). Pod infection results in blackened shriveled seeds and premature shattering.. Favorable weather: Temperature 15-25°C with intermittent showers and overcast sky..

title: Disease: Red Rot in Sugarcane
content: Disease: Red Rot (ఎర్ర కుళ్లు తెగులు (కాల్చే తెగులు), गन्ने का लाल सड़न रोग) in Sugarcane. Pathogen: Fungal (Colletotrichum falcatum). Symptoms: Yellowing and withering of third or fourth leaf from crown. Splitting the cane longitudinally reveals crimson-red pith interspersed with characteristic white crosswise bands and alcoholic odor.. Favorable weather: Waterlogged poorly drained soils, continuous ratooning, monsoon floodwaters..

title: Disease: Smut Disease in Sugarcane
content: Disease: Smut Disease (కాటుక తెగులు (స్మట్), कंडुआ रोग / स्मट) in Sugarcane. Pathogen: Fungal (Sporisorium scitamineum). Symptoms: Production of a prominent whip-like, curved, pencil-thick unbranched structure (up to 1.5m long) from apical meristem, covered with black sooty chlamydospores.. Favorable weather: Hot dry weather (30-35°C), infected setts, ratoon crops in dry soils..

title: Disease: Purple Blotch in Onion
content: Disease: Purple Blotch (ఊదా రంగు మచ్చ తెగులు, बैंगनी धब्बा रोग) in Onion. Pathogen: Fungal (Alternaria porri). Symptoms: Small, sunken, water-soaked lesions that rapidly expand into large elliptical purple-centered spots with yellow halo on leaves and seed stalks. Stalks break at the lesion.. Favorable weather: Warm temperature (25-30°C), relative humidity >85%, heavy thrips feeding punctures..

title: Disease: Late Blight in Potato
content: Disease: Late Blight (ఆలస్యపు తెగులు (ఆలూ లేట్ బ్లైట్), आलू पछेती झुलसा) in Potato. Pathogen: Oomycete (Phytophthora infestans). Symptoms: Water-soaked lesions on leaf margins turning black necrotic; white mildew growth on underside in morning. Tubers develop dry, rusty brown subterranean rot extending into flesh.. Favorable weather: Temperature 10-20°C, RH >90%, persistent dense fog or drizzling rainfall..
citation: ICAR-CPRI Shimla Late Blight Forecasting System 2025

title: Disease: Rhizome Rot / Soft Rot in Turmeric
content: Disease: Rhizome Rot / Soft Rot (దుంప కుళ్లు తెగులు, कंद सड़न रोग) in Turmeric. Pathogen: Oomycete / Fungal (Pythium aphanidermatum). Symptoms: Progressive yellowing of lower leaves from margins inwards. Pseudostem collar becomes soft and water-soaked, detaching easily with slight pull. Rhizomes rot into foul soft watery mass.. Favorable weather: Water stagnation, heavy soils with poor drainage, temperature 25-30°C during monsoon..

title: Disease: Colletotrichum Leaf Spot in Turmeric
content: Disease: Colletotrichum Leaf Spot (ఆకుమచ్చ తెగులు, पत्ती चित्ती रोग) in Turmeric. Pathogen: Fungal (Colletotrichum curcumae). Symptoms: Oblong to circular brown spots with grey center and dark brown margin appearing on both leaf surfaces. In advanced stages, spots coalesce drying out entire leaf lamina.. Favorable weather: High humidity (80-90%), cloudy days, intermittent rains in August-October..

title: Pest: Pink Bollworm in Cotton
content: Insect Pest: Pink Bollworm (గులాబీ రంగు కాయ తొలుచు పురుగు, गुलाबी सुंडी) in Cotton. Scientific name: Pectinophora gossypiella. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights OR 10% damaged green bolls (rosette flowers observed). Damage symptoms: Larvae bore into squares, flowers, and bolls. Attacked flowers show 'rosette flower' symptom where petals twist together. Bolls show premature drop, fiber staining, and locule burrowing.. Natural predators: Trichogramma bactrae, Bracon greeni, Chrysoperla zastrowi.

title: Pest: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) in Rice / Paddy
content: Insect Pest: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) (గోధుమ రంగు సుడిదోమ, भूरा फुदका) in Rice / Paddy. Scientific name: Nilaparvata lugens. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5-10 insects/hill at tillering; 15-20 insects/hill at panicle initiation. Damage symptoms: Both nymphs and adults congregate at base of plant and suck sap. Infested plants turn yellow and dry up rapidly, resulting in circular patches of dried crop called 'hopper burn'.. Natural predators: Mirid bug (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis), Wolf spider (Lycosa pseudoannulata).

title: Pest: Chilli Thrips in Chilli
content: Insect Pest: Chilli Thrips (మిరప నల్లి (తామర పురుగులు), मिर्च के थ्रिप्स) in Chilli. Scientific name: Scirtothrips dorsalis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 thrips per leaf or upward curling on 10% seedlings. Damage symptoms: Lacerate leaf surface and suck exudate. Leaves curl upwards (boat-shaped). Stunted plant growth, bronzing of leaves, reduced flower bud formation.. Natural predators: Anthocorid bugs (Orius tantillus), Green lacewing (Chrysoperla carnea).

title: Pest: Yellow Stem Borer in Rice / Paddy
content: Insect Pest: Yellow Stem Borer (వరి కాండం తొలిచే పురుగు, पीला तना छेदक) in Rice / Paddy. Scientific name: Scirpophaga incertulas. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 egg mass/sq.m or 5% dead hearts at vegetative stage; 1 moth/sq.m or 2% white ears at flowering. Damage symptoms: Larvae bore into central shoot causing 'dead heart' at vegetative stage (easily pulled out) and empty, erect white chaffy panicles ('white earhead') at reproductive stage.. Natural predators: Trichogramma japonicum, Tetrastichus schoenobii, Spiders.

title: Pest: Rice Leaf Folder in Rice / Paddy
content: Insect Pest: Rice Leaf Folder (వరి ఆకుచుట్టు పురుగు, पत्ती लपेटक) in Rice / Paddy. Scientific name: Cnaphalocrocis medinalis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 folded damaged leaves with larvae per hill. Damage symptoms: Larva folds leaf blade longitudinally and scrapes green chlorophyll from inside, creating longitudinal transparent white streaks. Severe infestation gives field a scorched white look.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Damselflies, Ground beetles.

title: Pest: Whitefly in Cotton
content: Insect Pest: Whitefly (తెల్లదోమ, सफेद मक्खी) in Cotton. Scientific name: Bemisia tabaci. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 6-8 adults or nymphs per leaf on upper/middle canopy. Damage symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck phloem sap, secrete sticky honeydew promoting black sooty mold growth on leaves and lint. Acts as principal vector for Cotton Leaf Curl Virus (CLCuV).. Natural predators: Chrysoperla zastrowi, Coccinella septempunctata, Encarsia formosa.

title: Pest: Jassids / Leafhopper in Cotton
content: Insect Pest: Jassids / Leafhopper (పచ్చదోమ, हरा तेला / फुदका) in Cotton. Scientific name: Amrasca biguttula biguttula. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 nymphs per leaf or downward cupping of leaf margin (Grade II injury). Damage symptoms: Nymphs walk sideways on underside of leaves and suck sap while injecting toxic saliva. Leaf margins turn yellow, then bronze/brick red, curl downward ('hopper burn').. Natural predators: Ladybird beetles, Spider guild (Oxyopes salticus).

title: Pest: American Bollworm in Cotton
content: Insect Pest: American Bollworm (శనగపచ్చ పురుగు, अमेरिकन सुंडी) in Cotton. Scientific name: Helicoverpa armigera. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 larva per plant or 5% damaged squares/bolls. Damage symptoms: Caterpillar feeds on squares and green bolls thrusting head inside while keeping rest of body outside. Clean circular boreholes surrounded by fecal pellets.. Natural predators: Campoletis chloridae, HaNPV, Trichogramma chilonis.

title: Pest: Yellow Mite / Broad Mite in Chilli
content: Insect Pest: Yellow Mite / Broad Mite (నల్ల తామర / ఎర్ర నల్లి (పసుపు నల్లి), पीली माइट) in Chilli. Scientific name: Polyphagotarsonemus latus. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 2-3 mites per leaf on top canopy. Damage symptoms: Mites suck sap from tender shoots. Leaves curl downwards (inverted boat shape / inverted cup), elongate into 'rat-tail' symptom with thickened dark green leathery texture.. Natural predators: Phytoseiid predatory mites (Amblyseius swirskii, Neoseiulus longispinosus).

title: Pest: Tobacco Caterpillar in Chilli
content: Insect Pest: Tobacco Caterpillar (లద్దె పురుగు, तंबाकू की इल्ली) in Chilli. Scientific name: Spodoptera litura. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 egg mass or 1 skeletonized leaf patch per 10 plants. Damage symptoms: Gregarious early instar caterpillars skeletonize leaves leaving parchment-like veins. Later instars voraciously defoliate plants, cut stems, and bore into chilli pods.. Natural predators: SlNPV, Bracon hebetor, Canthecona furcellata.

title: Pest: Tomato Fruit Borer in Tomato
content: Insect Pest: Tomato Fruit Borer (టమోటా కాయ తొలిచే పురుగు, टमाटर फल छेदक) in Tomato. Scientific name: Helicoverpa armigera. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 larva/plant or 5% fruit damage. Damage symptoms: Larvae bore into green and ripening fruits making round holes, leading to entry of rot pathogens and fruit dropping.. Natural predators: Trichogramma pretiosum, Chrysoperla carnea.

title: Pest: Tomato Pinworm / Leaf Miner in Tomato
content: Insect Pest: Tomato Pinworm / Leaf Miner (టమోటా పిన్ వార్మ్, टमाटर पिनवर्म) in Tomato. Scientific name: Tuta absoluta. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 active mines per leaf or 20-30 moths/pheromone trap/week. Damage symptoms: Larvae feed as leaf miners creating large transparent blotches (mines) in leaf mesophyll. Also bore into growing buds, stems, and fruits leaving pinhole puncture marks.. Natural predators: Nesidiocoris tenuis, Trichogramma achaeae.

title: Pest: Wheat Aphids in Wheat
content: Insect Pest: Wheat Aphids (గోధుమ పేనుబంక, गेहूं का माहू / चेपा) in Wheat. Scientific name: Rhopalosiphum padi & Sitobion avenae. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 10-15 aphids per earhead / tiller at heading stage. Damage symptoms: Colonies of aphids suck sap from leaves, flag leaf sheath, and developing earheads, resulting in chaffy ears, shriveled grains, and reduced test weight.. Natural predators: Coccinella septempunctata, Syrphid fly larvae (Episyrphus balteatus).

title: Pest: Termites in Wheat
content: Insect Pest: Termites (చెదలు, दीमक) in Wheat. Scientific name: Odontotermes obesus & Microtermes obesi. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): Presence of fresh soil galleries and wilting seedlings in patches. Damage symptoms: Termites feed on underground roots and stem base of germinating seedlings and mature plants, causing yellowing, drying, and lodging; affected tillers pull out easily.. Natural predators: Formicid predatory ants.

title: Pest: Fall Armyworm (FAW) in Maize
content: Insect Pest: Fall Armyworm (FAW) (కత్తెర పురుగు, फॉल आर्मीवॉर्म / सैनिक कीट) in Maize. Scientific name: Spodoptera frugiperda. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5% damaged plants with larvae at early whorl; 10% at mid-whorl stage. Damage symptoms: Pinholes and large irregular papery windowpanes on whorl leaves. Deep feeding inside central whorl with excessive sawdust-like fecal frass accumulation. Destroys growing point ('dead heart').. Natural predators: Earwig (Euborellia annulipes), Telenomus remus, Nomuraea rileyi.
citation: ICAR-IIMR & DPPQS Fall Armyworm National Campaign 2025

title: Pest: Maize Stem Borer in Maize
content: Insect Pest: Maize Stem Borer (మొక్కజొన్న కాండం తొలిచే పురుగు, मक्का तना छेदक) in Maize. Scientific name: Chilo partellus. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 10% plants showing pinholes or dead hearts. Damage symptoms: Shot holes in leaf whorls; larvae bore into central shoots causing vegetative dead hearts. In later stages, tunnels through stalks causing stem breakage and lodging.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Cotesia flavipes.

title: Pest: Groundnut Leaf Miner in Groundnut / Peanut
content: Insect Pest: Groundnut Leaf Miner (వేరుశనగ ఆకుముడుత / ఆకుతొలుచు పురుగు, मूंगफली पत्ती सुरंगक) in Groundnut / Peanut. Scientific name: Aproaerema modicella. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5 active larvae per plant or 20% damaged leaves. Damage symptoms: Larvae mine into tender leaflets creating blister-like mines. Later instars web leaflets together and feed within, giving the entire crop a scorched brownish appearance.. Natural predators: Bracon gelechiae, Goniozus sp..

title: Pest: Red Hairy Caterpillar in Groundnut / Peanut
content: Insect Pest: Red Hairy Caterpillar (ఎర్ర గొంగళి పురుగు, लाल रोएंदार इल्ली) in Groundnut / Peanut. Scientific name: Amsacta albistriga. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 egg masses or 8 larvae per 10-meter row. Damage symptoms: Gregarious caterpillars migrate en masse across fields completely devastating green vegetation down to ground level within hours.. Natural predators: Ground beetles (Calosoma sp.), Predatory birds.

title: Pest: White Grub in Groundnut / Peanut
content: Insect Pest: White Grub (తెల్ల పురుగు / వేరు పురుగు, सफेद लट) in Groundnut / Peanut. Scientific name: Holotrichia consanguinea. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 grub per square meter in soil. Damage symptoms: C-shaped fleshy white grubs chew taproots underground. Infested plants turn pale, wilt, and die in scattered patches; pull out effortlessly.. Natural predators: Metarhizium anisopliae, Beauveria brongniartii.

title: Pest: Girdle Beetle in Soybean
content: Insect Pest: Girdle Beetle (రింగ్ బీటిల్ (కాండం కొరికే పురుగు), गर्डल बीटल / चक्र भृंग) in Soybean. Scientific name: Obereopsis brevis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5-10% plants showing girdled stems. Damage symptoms: Female beetle makes two parallel ring cuts around petiole or stem and oviposits between them. Plant portion above ring withers and droops; larva tunnels downward inside pith.. Natural predators: Parasitic wasps, Entomopathogenic fungi.

title: Pest: Semilooper in Soybean
content: Insect Pest: Semilooper (పచ్చ గొంగళి పురుగు, अर्धकुंडलक इल्ली (सेमीलूपर)) in Soybean. Scientific name: Thysanoplusia orichalcea & Chrysodeixis acuta. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 3-4 larvae per meter row length. Damage symptoms: Larvae walk with looping motion and consume leaf lamina leaving only veins and midribs, leading to heavy defoliation during flowering and pod development.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Bacillus thuringiensis, Nomuraea rileyi.

title: Pest: Gram Pod Borer in Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Insect Pest: Gram Pod Borer (శనగపచ్చ పురుగు (కంది కాయ తొలిచే పురుగు), अरहर फली छेदक) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea. Scientific name: Helicoverpa armigera. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 larva per plant or 5% pod damage. Damage symptoms: Larvae bore into developing pods, consume green seeds from inside, leaving large circular bore holes and dropping frass outside.. Natural predators: Campoletis chloridae, HaNPV, Spiders.

title: Pest: Pigeonpea Pod Fly in Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Insect Pest: Pigeonpea Pod Fly (కాయ ఈగ, फली मक्खी) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea. Scientific name: Melanagromyza obtusa. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5-10% infested green pods. Damage symptoms: Maggots feed inside green seeds without external symptoms until adult fly cuts an exit hole window before emerging; damaged seeds lose germination and market value.. Natural predators: Euderus agromyzae, Ormyrus orientalis.

title: Pest: Gram Pod Borer in Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Insect Pest: Gram Pod Borer (శనగ కాయ తొలిచే పురుగు, चना फली छेदक) in Chickpea / Bengal Gram. Scientific name: Helicoverpa armigera. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 larva per meter row or 1 moth/pheromone trap/day. Damage symptoms: Larva feeds on tender leaflets in vegetative stage, then defoliates flowers and bores into developing pods, eating developing seeds and reducing yield by up to 50%.. Natural predators: Campoletis chloridae, Trichogramma chilonis, HaNPV.

title: Pest: Mustard Aphid in Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Insect Pest: Mustard Aphid (ఆవాల పేనుబంక, सरसों का माहू / चेपा) in Mustard / Rapeseed. Scientific name: Lipaphis erysimi. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 20-25% plants infested or 1.5 - 2.0 cm aphid colony on central shoot tip. Damage symptoms: Dense colonies of small greenish aphids suck sap from inflorescence, floral buds, and pods, curling flowers and resulting in pod shriveling and poor oil content.. Natural predators: Ladybird beetle (Coccinella septempunctata), Syrphid larvae.

title: Pest: Mustard Sawfly in Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Insect Pest: Mustard Sawfly (ఆవాల రంపపు ఈగ, सरसों की आरा मक्खी) in Mustard / Rapeseed. Scientific name: Athalia lugens proxima. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1 larva per square meter or 2 larvae per plant at seedling stage. Damage symptoms: Greenish-black cylindrical larvae feed on leaves from edges towards midrib making large irregular holes, causing complete defoliation of young seedlings.. Natural predators: Perilampus microgastri, Ground predators.

title: Pest: Early Shoot Borer in Sugarcane
content: Insect Pest: Early Shoot Borer (చెరకు మొవ్వు తొలిచే పురుగు, शुरुआती प्ररोह छेदक) in Sugarcane. Scientific name: Chilo infuscatellus. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 15% dead hearts during formative stage (up to 120 DAP). Damage symptoms: Larva enters below ground level and tunnels upward, destroying central spindle and producing foul-smelling 'dead heart' that pulls out easily.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis (release @ 50,000/ha), Granulosis virus (ESB-GV).

title: Pest: Sugarcane Top Borer in Sugarcane
content: Insect Pest: Sugarcane Top Borer (చెరకు పై మొవ్వు తొలిచే పురుగు, चोटी छेदक) in Sugarcane. Scientific name: Scirpophaga excerptalis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 10% dead hearts or presence of red shot holes on leaf midribs. Damage symptoms: Shot holes on leaves, red tunnel along leaf midrib, destruction of growing tip resulting in bunchy top appearance with profuse lateral sprouting.. Natural predators: Rhaconotus scirpophagae, Trichogramma japonicum.

title: Pest: Onion Thrips in Onion
content: Insect Pest: Onion Thrips (ఉల్లి తామర పురుగులు, प्याज के थ्रिप्स) in Onion. Scientific name: Thrips tabaci. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 30 thrips per plant at vegetative / bulb initiation stage. Damage symptoms: Adults and nymphs congregate in leaf sheath axils, rasp epidermal tissues creating silvery white blotches and streaks. Leaves distort, dry from tip down, reducing bulb size.. Natural predators: Chrysoperla carnea, Aeolothrips intermedius.

title: Pest: Potato Tuber Moth (PTM) in Potato
content: Insect Pest: Potato Tuber Moth (PTM) (ఆలూ దుంప తొలిచే పురుగు, आलू कंद शलभ) in Potato. Scientific name: Phthorimaea operculella. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5% leaf infestation in field or 2-4 moths/pheromone trap/week in store. Damage symptoms: In field, larvae mine leaves and tunnel through petioles into exposed tubers. In country stores, caterpillars bore winding tunnels through tubers filled with dark silken frass.. Natural predators: Copidosoma koehleri, Chelonus blackburni.

title: Pest: Turmeric Shoot Borer in Turmeric
content: Insect Pest: Turmeric Shoot Borer (పసుపు కాండం తొలిచే పురుగు, हल्दी प्ररोह छेदक) in Turmeric. Scientific name: Conogethes punctiferalis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5% dead hearts or bore holes on pseudostems. Damage symptoms: Larvae bore into pseudostems and feed internally, resulting in yellowing and drying of central shoot ('dead heart'). Frass extrudes from boreholes.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Bracon brevicornis.

title: Pest: Rhizome Scale in Turmeric
content: Insect Pest: Rhizome Scale (పసుపు పొలుసు పురుగు, कंद शल्क कीट) in Turmeric. Scientific name: Aspidiotus hartii. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): Presence of white circular scales on seed rhizomes before storage/planting. Damage symptoms: Circular greyish-white scales encrust rhizomes in storage and field, sucking sap, leading to shriveling, desiccation, and complete loss of germination.. Natural predators: Chilocorus nigrita, Encarsia citrina.

title: Pest: Rice Gall Midge in Rice / Paddy
content: Insect Pest: Rice Gall Midge (వరి ఉల్లికోడు / ఆనెకోడు పురుగు, गाल मिज / पोंगा कीट) in Rice / Paddy. Scientific name: Orseolia oryzae. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5% silver shoots at tillering stage. Damage symptoms: Maggot feeds at growing tip of apical meristem, transforming leaf sheath into a hollow, tubular silvery-white gall called 'silver shoot' or 'onion leaf', preventing panicle formation.. Natural predators: Platygaster oryzae, Neanastatus grallarius.

title: Pest: Rice Earhead Bug / Gundhi Bug in Rice / Paddy
content: Insect Pest: Rice Earhead Bug / Gundhi Bug (వరి వెన్ను నల్లి, गंधी बग) in Rice / Paddy. Scientific name: Leptocorisa acuta. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 1-2 bugs per hill or 5 bugs per sq. meter at milking stage. Damage symptoms: Nymphs and adults suck milky sap from developing grains during early morning and evening hours. Grains become empty, spotted brown, or chaffy, giving off an unpleasant buggy smell.. Natural predators: Spiders, Predatory crickets.

title: Pest: Whitefly & Pod Borer Complex in Black Gram / Urad
content: Insect Pest: Whitefly & Pod Borer Complex (తెల్లదోమ మరియు కాయ తొలిచే పురుగు, सफेद मक्खी एवं फली छेदक) in Black Gram / Urad. Scientific name: Bemisia tabaci & Maruca vitrata. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 5 whiteflies per leaf or 5% webbed flowers/pods. Damage symptoms: Whiteflies transmit Mungbean Yellow Mosaic Virus; Maruca larvae web flowers and pods together, feeding internally on seeds.. Natural predators: Trichogramma chilonis, Ladybird beetles.

title: Pest: Sugarcane Whitefly in Sugarcane
content: Insect Pest: Sugarcane Whitefly (చెరకు తెల్లదోమ, गन्ने की सफेद मक्खी) in Sugarcane. Scientific name: Aleurolobus barodensis. Economic Threshold Level (ETL): 20-25 nymphs/puparia per square inch on lower leaf surface. Damage symptoms: Nymphs suck sap from underside of leaves; leaves turn yellow and pinkish-purple, coated with black sooty mold; sucrose recovery drops by 1-2 units.. Natural predators: Chrysoperla zastrowi, Scymnus nubilus.

title: IPM Protocol: Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) in Cotton
content: IPM for Pink Bollworm (Pectinophora gossypiella) on Cotton. Cultural: Strict adherence to sowing window (June 15 - July 15); avoid long duration varieties; terminate crop by December to prevent off-season host carryover; deep summer ploughing.. Mechanical: Install delta/funnel pheromone traps @ 4-5 traps/acre for monitoring; 8-10 traps/acre for mass trapping; manual plucking and destroying of rosette flowers.. Biological: Release Trichogramma bactrae egg parasitoid @ 60,000 eggs/acre (3 tricho-cards) at 45 and 60 DAS; spray Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 1 liter/acre (5 ml/L) at early square stage.. ETL Monitoring: 8 moths/trap/night for 3 consecutive nights OR 10% rosette flowers.. Chemical last resort: Proclaim 5% SG (Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG) @ 88 g/acre (6.6 g per 15L pump) or Delegate 11.7% SC (Spinetoram) @ 170 ml/acre (13 ml per 15L pump)..
citation: NIPHM Hyderabad & ICAR-CICR Cotton IPM Strategy 2025

title: IPM Protocol: Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) in Rice / Paddy
content: IPM for Brown Plant Hopper (BPH) on Rice / Paddy. Cultural: Adopt 'alley formation' (skipping 1 row after every 8-10 rows) for aeration and sunlight; alternate wetting and drying (AWD) water management; avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer.. Mechanical: Drain water completely for 3-4 days when initial hopper colonies are observed; install light traps to monitor hopper flights.. Biological: Conserve predatory wolf spiders (Lycosa pseudoannulata) and mirid bugs (Cyrtorhinus lividipennis); avoid broad-spectrum pyrethroid sprays which cause BPH resurgence.. ETL Monitoring: 5-10 insects per hill at tillering; 15-20 insects per hill at panicle initiation.. Chemical last resort: Chess 50% WG (Pymetrozine 50% WG) @ 120 g/acre (9 g per 15L pump) or Token/Osheen 20% SG (Dinotefuran) @ 80-100 g/acre (6-7.5 g per 15L pump) directed at plant base..

title: IPM Protocol: Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas) in Rice / Paddy
content: IPM for Yellow Stem Borer (Scirpophaga incertulas) on Rice / Paddy. Cultural: Clip seedling leaf tips before transplanting to eliminate egg masses; synchronise planting; harvest crop close to ground level to eliminate overwintering larvae.. Mechanical: Install Scirpo-lure pheromone traps @ 4-5 traps/acre; collect and destroy egg masses during field inspection.. Biological: Release Trichogramma japonicum @ 40,000 eggs/acre (2 cards) twice at weekly intervals starting 30 DAT.. ETL Monitoring: 1 egg mass/sq.m or 5% dead hearts at vegetative stage; 2% white ears at flowering.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC (Chlorantraniliprole) @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump) or Caldan 50% SP (Cartap Hydrochloride) @ 400 g/acre (30 g per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Chilli Thrips & Yellow Mites in Chilli
content: IPM for Chilli Thrips & Yellow Mites on Chilli. Cultural: Grow 3-4 border rows of maize, sorghum or bajra as barrier crop; intercrop with coriander; maintain field sanitation free from solanaceous weeds.. Mechanical: Erect blue sticky traps @ 15-20 traps/acre for thrips and yellow sticky traps for whiteflies at crop canopy height.. Biological: Spray Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) or Azadirachtin 10000 ppm @ 1.5 ml/L; release predatory mites Amblyseius swirskii @ 10 mites/sq.m.. ETL Monitoring: 1-2 thrips per leaf or upward curling on 10% seedlings.. Chemical last resort: Pegasus 50% WP (Diafenthiuron 50% WP) @ 240 g/acre (18 g per 15L pump) for thrips; Oberon 22.9% SC (Spiromesifen) @ 200 ml/acre (15 ml per 15L pump) for mites..

title: IPM Protocol: Anthracnose & Fruit Rot (Colletotrichum capsici) in Chilli
content: IPM for Anthracnose & Fruit Rot (Colletotrichum capsici) on Chilli. Cultural: Use certified disease-free seeds; avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; collect and burn fallen infected fruits.. Mechanical: Raise plants on raised beds covered with silver-on-black polyethylene mulch to prevent soil splashing.. Biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed + Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed; foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L.. ETL Monitoring: First appearance of circular sunken spots on developing or ripening fruits.. Chemical last resort: Folicur 25.9% EC (Tebuconazole) @ 250 ml/acre (18 ml per 15L pump) or Amistar Top (Azoxystrobin + Difenoconazole) @ 200 ml/acre (15 ml per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Tomato Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) in Tomato
content: IPM for Tomato Fruit Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) on Tomato. Cultural: Plant African tall marigold (Tagetes erecta) as trap crop (1 row of marigold for every 16 rows of tomato).. Mechanical: Install Helilure pheromone traps @ 5 traps/acre; hand-pick and destroy initial bored fruits with caterpillars.. Biological: Release Trichogramma pretiosum @ 50,000 eggs/acre; spray HaNPV @ 250 LE/acre (1.5 ml/L) with 0.1% jaggery sticker in evening hours.. ETL Monitoring: 1 larva per plant or 5% fruit damage.. Chemical last resort: Fame 39.35% SC (Flubendiamide) @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump) or Coragen 18.5% SC @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Tomato Pinworm (Tuta absoluta) in Tomato
content: IPM for Tomato Pinworm (Tuta absoluta) on Tomato. Cultural: Use pest-free seedlings raised under 40-mesh nylon insect net nurseries; destroy crop residues immediately after final harvest.. Mechanical: Install Tuta pheromone water traps or delta traps @ 12-15 traps/acre; seal greenhouse vents with insect-proof netting.. Biological: Release mirid predator Nesidiocoris tenuis; foliar spray of Bacillus thuringiensis kurstaki (Btk) @ 2 g/L.. ETL Monitoring: 20-30 moths/trap/week or 1 active mine per leaf.. Chemical last resort: Delegate 11.7% SC (Spinetoram) @ 180 ml/acre (13.5 ml per 15L pump) or Coragen 18.5% SC @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) in Maize
content: IPM for Fall Armyworm (Spodoptera frugiperda) on Maize. Cultural: Synchronised community planting within 2-week window; intercrop with cowpea or pigeonpea; avoid staggered sowing.. Mechanical: Hand-picking and crushing of egg masses and young larvae; apply dry fine sand or wood ash into whorls of attacked plants to damage larval cuticle.. Biological: Erect T-shaped bird perches @ 15-20 per acre; spray Beauveria bassiana 1x10^8 CFU/g @ 1 kg/acre (5 g/L) or Metarhizium rileyi at early whorl stage.. ETL Monitoring: 5% damaged plants with larvae at seedling/early whorl stage.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC (Chlorantraniliprole) @ 80 ml/acre (6 ml per 15L pump) or Delegate 11.7% SC @ 170 ml/acre directed into leaf whorls..

title: IPM Protocol: Sucking Pests (Whitefly, Jassids, Thrips) in Cotton
content: IPM for Sucking Pests (Whitefly, Jassids, Thrips) on Cotton. Cultural: Grow border rows of sorghum/bajra (3 rows) as barrier; avoid excessive chemical urea application which triggers vegetative succulence.. Mechanical: Install yellow sticky traps (for whiteflies/jassids) and blue sticky traps (for thrips) @ 15-20 traps/acre.. Biological: Release green lacewing Chrysoperla zastrowi @ 4,000 larvae/acre; foliar spray of Verticillium lecanii @ 1 kg/acre.. ETL Monitoring: 6-8 whiteflies/leaf; 2 jassids/leaf; 5 thrips/leaf.. Chemical last resort: Token/Osheen 20% SG (Dinotefuran) @ 60-80 g/acre (4.5-6 g per 15L pump) or Actara 25% WG (Thiamethoxam) @ 40 g/acre (3 g per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) in Rice / Paddy
content: IPM for Rice Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae) on Rice / Paddy. Cultural: Use resistant / tolerant varieties (RNR 15048, MTU 1010, BPT 5204 with seed treatment); avoid over-application of nitrogen; apply nitrogen in 3 split doses.. Mechanical: Maintain thin film of water; avoid drought stress as dry soil condition drastically escalates blast susceptibility.. Biological: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed + foliar spray @ 5 g/L at maximum tillering.. ETL Monitoring: 1-2 spindle-shaped lesions per hill on leaves or initial neck infection signs.. Chemical last resort: Amistar Top (Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC) @ 200 ml/acre (15 ml per 15L pump) or Nativo 75% WG (Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole) @ 80 g/acre (6 g per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Tikka Leaf Spot & Collar Rot in Groundnut / Peanut
content: IPM for Tikka Leaf Spot & Collar Rot on Groundnut / Peanut. Cultural: Crop rotation with non-legumes (sorghum, pearl millet, maize); clean cultivation by destroying crop residues.. Mechanical: Maintain optimal plant population; ensure adequate drainage to avoid collar water stagnation.. Biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed; application of 1 kg Trichoderma enriched in 100 kg FYM per acre into soil at sowing.. ETL Monitoring: Initial leaf lesions observed at 40-45 DAS.. Chemical last resort: Custodia / Harpul (Tebuconazole 10% + Sulphur 65% WG) @ 500 g/acre (37.5 g per 15L pump) or Saaf (Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP) @ 300 g/acre (22 g per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Girdle Beetle & Semilooper in Soybean
content: IPM for Girdle Beetle & Semilooper on Soybean. Cultural: Plant recommended varieties; maintain plant spacing of 45x5 cm; deep summer ploughing to expose pupae to predatory birds.. Mechanical: Hand-pick and destroy girdled shoots containing eggs and young larvae at early stage.. Biological: Erect T-shaped bird perches @ 15-20 per acre; spray Bacillus thuringiensis var. kurstaki @ 400 g/acre (3 g/L).. ETL Monitoring: 5% plants showing girdled rings or 3-4 semilooper larvae per meter row.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC (Chlorantraniliprole) @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump) or Ampligo (Chlorantraniliprole 9.3% + Lambda-cyhalothrin 4.6% ZC) @ 80 ml/acre..

title: IPM Protocol: Pod Borer Complex (Helicoverpa & Maruca) in Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: IPM for Pod Borer Complex (Helicoverpa & Maruca) on Red Gram / Pigeonpea. Cultural: Intercrop with sorghum, maize or green gram; plant trap crops (marigold); maintain wider row spacing (120-150 cm).. Mechanical: Install Helilure pheromone traps @ 5 traps/acre; shake plants early in morning over cloth sheets to dislodge and collect larvae.. Biological: Release Trichogramma chilonis @ 40,000 eggs/acre at flower bud stage; spray HaNPV @ 200 LE/acre + 0.5 kg jaggery in evening.. ETL Monitoring: 1 larva per plant or 5% pod damage.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC @ 60 ml/acre (4.5 ml per 15L pump) or Fame 39.35% SC (Flubendiamide) @ 40 ml/acre (3 ml per 15L pump) at 50% flowering..

title: IPM Protocol: Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) in Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: IPM for Gram Pod Borer (Helicoverpa armigera) on Chickpea / Bengal Gram. Cultural: Intercrop with coriander, mustard or linseed (4:1 row ratio); early sowing in October to escape heavy terminal pod borer attack.. Mechanical: Erect bird perches @ 20 T-perches/acre; install Helilure pheromone traps @ 4-5 traps/acre.. Biological: Spray HaNPV @ 200 LE/acre (1.5 ml/L) or Neem Seed Kernel Extract (NSKE 5%) at pod initiation stage.. ETL Monitoring: 1 larva per meter row or 5-10% pod damage.. Chemical last resort: Proclaim 5% SG (Emamectin Benzoate 5% SG) @ 80-88 g/acre (6-6.6 g per 15L pump) or Coragen 18.5% SC @ 50 ml/acre..

title: IPM Protocol: Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) in Mustard / Rapeseed
content: IPM for Mustard Aphid (Lipaphis erysimi) on Mustard / Rapeseed. Cultural: Sow timely before October 25 to enable crop to pass vulnerable flowering stage before peak aphid immigration in January.. Mechanical: Install yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 traps/acre; pluck and destroy initial aphid-infested floral twigs.. Biological: Conserve predatory Coccinellid beetles (Coccinella septempunctata) and syrphid fly maggots; spray Verticillium lecanii @ 1 kg/acre.. ETL Monitoring: 20% plants infested or 1.5 cm aphid colony on central shoot.. Chemical last resort: Actara 25% WG (Thiamethoxam 25% WG) @ 40-50 g/acre (3.5 g per 15L pump) or Rogor 30% EC (Dimethoate) @ 250-300 ml/acre (20 ml per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Early Shoot Borer (Chilo infuscatellus) in Sugarcane
content: IPM for Early Shoot Borer (Chilo infuscatellus) on Sugarcane. Cultural: Plant setts in deep trenches; apply light frequent irrigations during hot summer months; earthing-up at 45 and 90 DAP.. Mechanical: Trash mulching (10 cm thick dry sugarcane trash) across rows at 3 DAP to conserve soil moisture and prevent borer oviposition.. Biological: Release Trichogramma chilonis egg parasitoid @ 50,000/ha (2.5 cards) weekly 4-6 times from 30 DAP.. ETL Monitoring: 15% dead hearts during formative stage.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC (Chlorantraniliprole) @ 150 ml/acre applied as directed soil drench along cane row at 30-45 DAP..

title: IPM Protocol: Onion Thrips & Purple Blotch in Onion
content: IPM for Onion Thrips & Purple Blotch on Onion. Cultural: Grow two rows of maize or outer barrier of barrier crops; avoid water stress during bulb enlargement; crop rotation with non-allium crops.. Mechanical: Install blue and yellow sticky traps @ 20 traps/acre; overhead sprinkler irrigation reduces thrips population by mechanical dislodging.. Biological: Spray Beauveria bassiana 1x10^8 CFU/g @ 1 kg/acre (5 g/L) with sticker; Trichoderma viride seed and seedling dip.. ETL Monitoring: 30 thrips per plant or initial purple spots on foliage.. Chemical last resort: Pegasus 50% WP (Diafenthiuron) @ 240 g/acre (18 g per 15L pump) + Custodia (Tebuconazole + Azoxystrobin) @ 300 ml/acre (22 ml per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) in Potato
content: IPM for Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans) on Potato. Cultural: Use certified disease-free seed tubers from trusted seed source (CPRI); destroy cull piles and volunteer potato plants.. Mechanical: High earthing-up to ensure 10-15 cm soil cover over tubers preventing spore wash-down from foliage to tubers.. Biological: Prophylactic spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L before onset of cloudy fog weather.. ETL Monitoring: First appearance of water-soaked blighted lesions on leaf margins in locality.. Chemical last resort: Preventive: Dithane M-45 (Mancozeb 75% WP) @ 600-800 g/acre (50 g per 15L pump); Curative: Ridomil Gold (Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP) @ 500 g/acre (37.5 g per 15L pump)..

title: IPM Protocol: Rhizome Rot (Pythium aphanidermatum) in Turmeric
content: IPM for Rhizome Rot (Pythium aphanidermatum) on Turmeric. Cultural: Select disease-free seed rhizomes; provide excellent field drainage; plant on raised broad beds (120 cm width); incorporate neem cake @ 200 kg/acre.. Mechanical: Apply green leaf mulch (5 tonnes/acre) at planting and repeat at 45 and 90 DAP to conserve moisture and suppress pathogens.. Biological: Rhizome treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/kg rhizome for 30 min before planting; soil application of 2 kg Trichoderma in 200 kg FYM/acre.. ETL Monitoring: First collar water-soaking or leaf yellowing symptoms.. Chemical last resort: Drench collar region with Ridomil Gold (Metalaxyl 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP) @ 2.5 g/L or Copper Oxychloride 50% WP (Blitox) @ 3 g/L..

title: IPM Protocol: Yellow / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis) in Wheat
content: IPM for Yellow / Stripe Rust (Puccinia striiformis) on Wheat. Cultural: Grow resistant varieties (HD-3086, DBW-187, DBW-222, PBW-725); avoid early sowing of susceptible varieties in foothills of Himalayas.. Mechanical: Participatory surveillance and stripe rust scouting from December to February.. Biological: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed to boost systemic plant vigor.. ETL Monitoring: First isolated yellow stripe pustule colony detected in field.. Chemical last resort: Tilt 25% EC (Propiconazole 25% EC) @ 200 ml/acre (15 ml per 15L pump) in 200 liters water immediately upon detection..

title: IPM Protocol: Yellow Mosaic Virus & Maruca Pod Borer in Black Gram / Urad
content: IPM for Yellow Mosaic Virus & Maruca Pod Borer on Black Gram / Urad. Cultural: Use YMV resistant varieties (PU 31, VBN 8, WBG 26); destroy alternate weed hosts like Croton bonplandianum.. Mechanical: Erect yellow sticky traps @ 15-20 traps/acre to trap whitefly vectors early.. Biological: Seed treatment with Imidacloprid 600 FS (5 ml/kg seed) followed by foliar spray of Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 2 ml/L.. ETL Monitoring: 5 whiteflies per leaf or 5% webbed flowers/pods.. Chemical last resort: Coragen 18.5% SC @ 50 ml/acre (3.5 ml per 15L pump) for Maruca; Actara 25% WG @ 40 g/acre for whitefly vector..
