content: CIBRC Approved Use: Ridomil Gold (Metalaxyl-M 4% + Mancozeb 64% WP) on Potato against Late Blight. Dosage/Acre: 500 g (approx 37.5 g per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 1250 g. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 14 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Curative oomycete control. Alternate with non-phenylamide fungicides to avoid resistance..

title: Statutory Label: Oberon 22.9% SC for Chilli
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Oberon 22.9% SC (Spiromesifen 22.9% SC) on Chilli against Yellow Mite / Broad Mite. Dosage/Acre: 200 ml (approx 15.0 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 500 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 5 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Lipid biosynthesis inhibitor. Toxic to aquatic organisms. Dispose empty packing safely..

title: Statutory Label: Regent 5% SC for Rice / Paddy
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Regent 5% SC (Fipronil 5% SC) on Rice / Paddy against Yellow Stem Borer. Dosage/Acre: 400 ml (approx 30.0 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 1000 - 1500 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 32 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Do not spray near apiaries or while crop is in bloom. Toxic to aquatic invertebrates..

title: Statutory Label: Confidor 17.8% SL for Cotton
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Confidor 17.8% SL (Imidacloprid 17.8% SL) on Cotton against Jassids / Leafhopper. Dosage/Acre: 50 ml (approx 3.75 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 100 - 125 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 40 days. Toxicity: yellow_highly_toxic. Safety: Strictly observe 40-day PHI. Do not apply when honeybees are foraging..

title: Statutory Label: Stomp 30% EC for Cotton
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Stomp 30% EC (Pendimethalin 30% EC) on Cotton against Annual Grasses & Broadleaf Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 1000 ml (approx 75.0 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 2500 - 3300 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 90 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Must be applied onto moist soil surface. Do not disturb soil layer after application..

title: Statutory Label: Rifit 50% EC for Rice / Paddy
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Rifit 50% EC (Pretilachlor 50% EC) on Rice / Paddy against Barnyard Grass & Sedge Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 500 ml (approx 37.5 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 1000 - 1500 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 75 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Maintain 2-3 cm standing water for 48 hours after application for herbicide film formation..

title: Statutory Label: Atrataf 50% WP for Maize
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Atrataf 50% WP (Atrazine 50% WP) on Maize against Grassy & Broadleaf Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 500 g (approx 37.5 g per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 1000 - 2000 g. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 60 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Do not use in intercropping systems with pulses or oilseeds due to carryover injury..

title: Statutory Label: Nominee Gold 10% SC for Rice / Paddy
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Nominee Gold 10% SC (Bispyribac-sodium 10% SC) on Rice / Paddy against Grasses, Sedges & Broadleaf Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 80 ml (approx 6.0 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 200 - 250 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 45 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Do not spray on drought-stressed rice. Always apply with flat-fan nozzle..

title: Statutory Label: Targa Super 5% EC for Soybean
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Targa Super 5% EC (Quizalofop-ethyl 5% EC) on Soybean against Narrow Leaf Grassy Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 350 ml (approx 26.25 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 750 - 1000 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 30 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Selective graminicide. Safe to broadleaf crops. Do not spray against wind direction..

title: Statutory Label: Pursuit 10% SL for Groundnut / Peanut
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Pursuit 10% SL (Imazethapyr 10% SL) on Groundnut / Peanut against Grasses & Broadleaf Weeds. Dosage/Acre: 350 ml (approx 26.25 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 750 - 1000 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 60 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Ensure sufficient soil moisture at application. Wear protective rubber apron and boots..

title: Statutory Label: Sempra 75% WG for Sugarcane
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Sempra 75% WG (Halosulfuron-methyl 75% WG) on Sugarcane against Purple Nutsedge (Cyperus rotundus). Dosage/Acre: 36 g (approx 2.7 g per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 90 g. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 60 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Translocates into underground nuts and tubers inhibiting ALS enzyme. Use with non-ionic surfactant..

title: Statutory Label: Topik 15% WP for Wheat
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Topik 15% WP (Clodinafop-propargyl 15% WP) on Wheat against Phalaris minor (Canary Grass). Dosage/Acre: 160 g (approx 12.0 g per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 400 g. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 60 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Mix with supplied surfactant only. Do not mix with 2,4-D amine as antagonism occurs..

title: Statutory Label: Kasu-B for Rice / Paddy
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Kasu-B (Kasugamycin 3% SL) on Rice / Paddy against Bacterial Leaf Blight (BLB). Dosage/Acre: 400 ml (approx 30.0 ml per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 1000 - 1250 ml. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 30 days. Toxicity: green_slightly_toxic. Safety: Antibiotic bactericide and fungicide. Safe to fish and mammals. Wash container thrice before disposal..

title: Statutory Label: Blitox 50% WP for Tomato
content: CIBRC Approved Use: Blitox 50% WP (Copper Oxychloride 50% WP) on Tomato against Early Blight. Dosage/Acre: 1000 g (approx 75.0 g per 15L backpack pump). Dosage/Ha: 2500 g. Dilution: 200 liters/acre (500 liters/ha). PHI: 10 days. Toxicity: blue_moderately_toxic. Safety: Incompatible with strongly acidic compounds. Wear protective eyewear..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Cotton
content: Nutrient Management for Cotton: RDF: 60 : 30 : 30 kg (Bt Cotton under irrigation) / 48 : 24 : 24 kg (Rainfed) NPK/acre (150 : 75 : 75 kg (Irrigated) / 120 : 60 : 60 kg (Rainfed) NPK/ha). Basal: Full dose of Phosphorus (DAP 65 kg or SSP 188 kg) + 1/4th Nitrogen (Urea 25 kg) + 1/3rd Potash (MOP 17 kg) applied in furrow at sowing.. Top dressing: Apply Nitrogen and Potash in 3 equal splits: 1st split at 20-25 DAS (squaring initiation), 2nd split at 45-50 DAS (peak squaring), 3rd split at 70-75 DAS (boll formation).. Micronutrients: {'magnesium_deficiency': 'Reddening of lower leaves (leaf reddening) between veins while veins remain green. Correction: Foliar spray of Magnesium Sulphate (MgSO4) @ 10 g/L (1%) + Urea @ 10 g/L at 45 and 65 DAS.', 'boron_deficiency': 'Square dropping, deformed bolls, petiole ring formation. Correction: Soil application of Borax @ 4 kg/acre or foliar spray of Solubor (Boron 20%) @ 1.0 - 1.5 g/L at flowering.', 'zinc_deficiency': 'Interveinal chlorosis in young leaves, shortened internodes (little leaf). Correction: Zinc Sulphate (ZnSO4 21%) @ 10 kg/acre basal or foliar spray of 2 g/L Chelated Zinc (EDTA-Zn 12%).'}. Biofertilizers: Azotobacter / Azospirillum @ 500 g/acre + Phosphate Solubilizing Bacteria (PSB) @ 500 g/acre mixed with 100 kg FYM applied near root zone..
citation: PJTSAU Cotton Nutrient Management Package & ICAR-CICR Nagpur 2025

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Rice / Paddy
content: Nutrient Management for Rice / Paddy: RDF: 48 : 24 : 24 kg (Kharif) / 60 : 30 : 30 kg (Rabi) NPK/acre (120 : 60 : 60 kg (Kharif) / 150 : 75 : 75 kg (Rabi) NPK/ha). Basal: Full dose of Phosphorus (DAP 52 kg) + 1/3rd Nitrogen (Urea 26 kg) + 1/2 dose of Potash (MOP 20 kg) incorporated into puddle soil before final leveling.. Top dressing: Remaining Nitrogen applied in 2 splits: 1st split (Urea 35 kg) at active tillering (20-25 DAT), 2nd split (Urea 35 kg) + remaining Potash (MOP 20 kg) at panicle initiation (45-50 DAT).. Micronutrients: {'zinc_deficiency_khaira_disease': 'Rusty-brown irregular pigmentation appearing on 3rd and 4th leaves 2-3 weeks after transplanting, stunted plant growth with brittle leaves. Correction: Basal soil application of Zinc Sulphate (21%) @ 20 kg/acre or foliar spray of Zinc Sulphate @ 2 g/L + 1 g/L slaked lime (twice at 5-day interval).', 'iron_deficiency': 'Interveinal chlorosis turning into bleached ivory-white leaves in light calcareous soils or dry direct-seeded rice (DSR). Correction: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 10 g/L (1%) + 1 g/L citric acid.'}. Biofertilizers: Azospirillum @ 1 kg/acre + PSB @ 1 kg/acre + Blue Green Algae (BGA) @ 4 kg/acre or Azolla dual cropping (incorporated at 30 DAT)..
citation: ICAR-IIRR Hyderabad Nutrient Bulletin & PJTSAU Vyavasaya Panchangam 2025

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Chilli
content: Nutrient Management for Chilli: RDF: 60 : 32 : 32 kg (Rainfed) / 120 : 48 : 48 kg (Irrigated hybrid chilli) NPK/acre (150 : 80 : 80 kg (Rainfed) / 300 : 120 : 120 kg (Irrigated) NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (SSP 200 kg or DAP 70 kg) + 1/5th Nitrogen (Urea 30 kg) + 1/3rd Potash (MOP 27 kg) applied in furrows along with 10 tonnes FYM.. Top dressing: Apply remaining Nitrogen in 4 equal splits at 30, 60, 90, and 120 DAT. Apply remaining Potash in 2 splits at 60 and 90 DAT.. Micronutrients: {'calcium_boron_deficiency': 'Blossom end rot in fruits and terminal bud necrosis. Correction: Foliar spray of Calcium Nitrate @ 5 g/L + Boron (Solubor) @ 1 g/L at fruit setting.', 'magnesium_deficiency': 'Interveinal yellowing of mature lower leaves. Correction: Foliar spray of Magnesium Sulphate @ 5 g/L.'}. Biofertilizers: VAM (Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhiza) @ 2 kg/acre in nursery + Azotobacter @ 1 kg/acre mixed with compost..
citation: PJTSAU Spices Agronomy Guide & ICAR-IIHR Bengaluru 2025

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Tomato
content: Nutrient Management for Tomato: RDF: 72 : 48 : 48 kg (Determinate) / 100 : 60 : 60 kg (Indeterminate staked hybrid) NPK/acre (180 : 120 : 120 kg (Determinate) / 250 : 150 : 150 kg (Staked) NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (DAP 100 kg) + 1/3rd Nitrogen (Urea 45 kg) + 1/2 Potash (MOP 40 kg) placed 10 cm deep in planting bed.. Top dressing: Top dress Nitrogen in 2 equal splits at 30 and 45 DAT. Apply remaining Potash at early fruit bulking (45 DAT). In fertigation: 19:19:19 @ 3 kg/acre weekly.. Micronutrients: {'blossom_end_rot_calcium': 'Dark, sunken, water-soaked, leathery black spots on blossom end of green fruits caused by localized calcium deficiency under fluctuating soil moisture. Correction: Foliar spray of Calcium Chloride @ 3 g/L or Calcium Nitrate @ 5 g/L weekly during fruit enlargement.', 'boron_deficiency': 'Fruit cracking, cat-facing, brittle petioles. Correction: Foliar spray of Solubor @ 1 g/L.'}. Biofertilizers: Azotobacter @ 1 kg/acre + PSB @ 1 kg/acre + Trichoderma harzianum @ 1 kg/acre in nursery potting media..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Wheat
content: Nutrient Management for Wheat: RDF: 48 : 24 : 16 kg (Timely sown irrigated) / 32 : 16 : 12 kg (Late sown) NPK/acre (120 : 60 : 40 kg (Timely) / 80 : 40 : 30 kg (Late) NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (DAP 52 kg) + Full Potash (MOP 27 kg) + 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 45 kg) drilled through ferti-seed drill at sowing.. Top dressing: Remaining 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 45 kg) top dressed in 2 equal splits: 1st split (22.5 kg) at Crown Root Initiation (CRI at 21 DAS) just before 1st irrigation; 2nd split (22.5 kg) at maximum tillering / first node stage (40-45 DAS).. Micronutrients: {'manganese_deficiency': 'Greyish-pink spots and interveinal chlorosis on middle leaves in light sandy soils under rice-wheat rotation. Correction: Foliar spray of 0.5% Manganese Sulphate (MnSO4 5 g/L) at 30 and 45 DAS.', 'zinc_deficiency': 'Brown necrotic spots on middle leaves. Correction: Basal application of Zinc Sulphate (21%) @ 10 kg/acre.'}. Biofertilizers: Azotobacter chroococcum @ 500 g/acre + PSB @ 500 g/acre seed inoculation..
citation: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal Wheat Nutrient Management Guide 2025

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Maize
content: Nutrient Management for Maize: RDF: 48 : 24 : 20 kg (Kharif) / 80 : 32 : 32 kg (Rabi / Winter hybrid maize) NPK/acre (120 : 60 : 50 kg (Kharif) / 200 : 80 : 80 kg (Rabi) NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (DAP 52 kg) + Full Potash (MOP 33 kg) + 1/3rd Nitrogen (Urea 30 kg) placed 5 cm away and below seed.. Top dressing: Apply remaining Nitrogen in 2 equal splits: 1st split (Urea 35 kg) at knee-high stage (30-35 DAS) followed by earthing up; 2nd split (Urea 35 kg) at tasseling / silking stage (55-60 DAS).. Micronutrients: {'zinc_deficiency_white_bud': "Bleaching or whitening of upper young leaves ('white bud of maize') starting from base of leaf. Correction: Soil application of 10 kg Zinc Sulphate (21%)/acre basal or foliar spray of Chelated Zinc @ 1 g/L."}. Biofertilizers: Azospirillum @ 1 kg/acre + PSB @ 1 kg/acre mixed with FYM..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Groundnut / Peanut
content: Nutrient Management for Groundnut / Peanut: RDF: 12 : 24 : 20 kg (Kharif) / 16 : 32 : 24 kg (Rabi / Summer) NPK/acre (30 : 60 : 50 kg (Kharif) / 40 : 80 : 60 kg (Rabi) NPK/ha). Basal: Entire dose of N, P, and K applied as basal at sowing (SSP 150 kg + Urea 20 kg + MOP 33 kg). SSP is mandatory as it provides 16% P2O5 and 12% Sulphur.. Top dressing: Gypsum application @ 200 kg/acre at pegging stage (40-45 DAS) placed 5-7 cm away from plant rows and incorporated into soil. Gypsum supplies essential Calcium and Sulphur for pod filling and prevents 'pops' (empty pods).. Micronutrients: {'iron_chlorosis': 'Complete yellowing to bleaching of young terminal leaves in high pH calcareous black soils. Correction: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 5 g/L + Citric acid @ 1 g/L twice at 7-day interval.', 'boron_deficiency_hollow_heart': 'Internal hollow cavity with dark discoloration inside kernel (hollow heart). Correction: Soil application of Borax @ 4 kg/acre or foliar spray of Solubor @ 1 g/L at 35 DAS.'}. Biofertilizers: Rhizobium (Bradyrhizobium sp.) @ 250 g / 10 kg seed + PSB @ 250 g/10 kg seed..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Soybean
content: Nutrient Management for Soybean: RDF: 12 : 32 : 16 kg (Basal application) NPK/acre (30 : 80 : 40 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Full dose of N, P, K applied basal at sowing. Use SSP (Single Super Phosphate) @ 200 kg/acre to meet both Phosphorus and Sulphur requirements + MOP @ 27 kg + Urea @ 15 kg as starter N.. Top dressing: Soybean fixes its own atmospheric nitrogen through Bradyrhizobium nodulation; no top dressing of urea is needed. Top dress Sulphur through elemental sulphur (10 kg/acre) if SSP was not used.. Micronutrients: {'zinc_deficiency': 'Yellowing between veins of upper leaves, bronze discoloration. Correction: Basal Zinc Sulphate @ 10 kg/acre or foliar spray of 0.5% ZnSO4.', 'molybdenum_deficiency': 'Poor nodulation and N-deficiency symptoms. Correction: Seed treatment with Sodium Molybdate @ 1 g/kg seed.'}. Biofertilizers: Bradyrhizobium japonicum @ 5 g/kg seed + PSB @ 5 g/kg seed mandatory..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Nutrient Management for Red Gram / Pigeonpea: RDF: 8 : 20 : 8 kg NPK/acre (20 : 50 : 20 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Entire fertilizer dose applied as basal placement below seed at sowing: DAP @ 45 kg + MOP @ 13 kg per acre.. Top dressing: Foliar spray of 2% Urea (20 g/L) or 2% DAP at flower bud initiation (70-80 DAS) and repeat 15 days later at peak flowering to reduce flower dropping and boost pod set.. Micronutrients: {'zinc_deficiency': 'Interveinal chlorosis of middle leaves. Correction: Foliar spray of Zinc Sulphate @ 2 g/L + lime 1 g/L.'}. Biofertilizers: Rhizobium culture @ 200 g / 8 kg seed + PSB culture @ 200 g/8 kg seed..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Nutrient Management for Chickpea / Bengal Gram: RDF: 8 : 20 : 8 kg NPK/acre (20 : 50 : 20 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Full dose placed 5-7 cm below seed at sowing using ferti-seed drill: DAP @ 45 kg + MOP @ 13 kg/acre.. Top dressing: No soil top dressing of nitrogen. Foliar spray of 2% Urea (20 g/L) or 1% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3 @ 10 g/L) at pod initiation (65-70 DAS) to enhance seed weight under receding residual moisture.. Micronutrients: {'iron_deficiency': 'Yellowing of terminal leaflets in high pH calcareous soils. Correction: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate (FeSO4) @ 5 g/L + Citric acid @ 1 g/L.'}. Biofertilizers: Mesorhizobium ciceri @ 250 g / 10 kg seed + PSB @ 250 g/10 kg seed..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Nutrient Management for Mustard / Rapeseed: RDF: 32 : 16 : 16 kg (Irrigated) / 20 : 12 : 10 kg (Rainfed) NPK/acre (80 : 40 : 40 kg (Irrigated) / 50 : 30 : 25 kg (Rainfed) NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (SSP 100 kg) + Full Potash (MOP 27 kg) + 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 30 kg) + Sulphur @ 16 kg/acre (through SSP or elemental sulphur).. Top dressing: Remaining 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 30 kg) top dressed after 1st irrigation at 30-35 DAS (before flowering).. Micronutrients: {'sulphur_deficiency': 'Cupping of young leaves, reddish-purple underside pigmentation, reduced pod siliquae formation and lower oil content. Correction: Basal application of Gypsum @ 100 kg/acre or Bentonite Sulphur (90%) @ 10 kg/acre.', 'boron_deficiency': 'Poor pod set, empty siliquae. Correction: Borax @ 4 kg/acre basal.'}. Biofertilizers: Azotobacter @ 500 g/acre + PSB @ 500 g/acre seed treatment..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Sugarcane
content: Nutrient Management for Sugarcane: RDF: 100 : 40 : 48 kg (Adsali/Pre-seasonal) / 80 : 32 : 40 kg (Suru / Spring cane) NPK/acre (250 : 100 : 120 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Apply 10% Nitrogen (Urea 18 kg) + Full Phosphorus (SSP 200 kg or DAP 70 kg) + 25% Potash (MOP 17 kg) in planting furrow along with 10 tonnes FYM/press mud.. Top dressing: Apply remaining Nitrogen and Potash in 3 splits: 1st split (20% N + 25% K) at tillering (45 DAP); 2nd split (30% N) at 90 DAP; 3rd split (40% N + 50% K) at final earthing-up (120-150 DAP). Stop all N application after 150 days.. Micronutrients: {'iron_chlorosis': 'Interveinal yellow striping of young cane leaves in alkaline soils. Correction: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulphate @ 10 g/L + Citric acid @ 1 g/L twice at 15-day intervals.', 'zinc_deficiency': 'Midrib bleaching and stunted internodes. Correction: Basal Zinc Sulphate @ 15 kg/acre.'}. Biofertilizers: Gluconacetobacter diazotrophicus (endophytic N-fixer) @ 2 kg/acre + PSB @ 2 kg/acre..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Onion
content: Nutrient Management for Onion: RDF: 40 : 20 : 32 kg + 20 kg Sulphur NPK/acre (100 : 50 : 80 kg + 50 kg Sulphur NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (SSP 125 kg) + 1/2 Potash (MOP 27 kg) + 1/3rd Nitrogen (Urea 25 kg) + Sulphur (Bentonite-S 10 kg) applied before transplanting.. Top dressing: Remaining Nitrogen top dressed in 2 equal splits: 1st split (Urea 30 kg) at 30 DAT; 2nd split (Urea 30 kg) + remaining Potash (MOP 27 kg) at 45-50 DAT (bulb initiation). Stop N application after 60 DAT to avoid thick necks.. Micronutrients: {'zinc_deficiency': 'Twisting, bending, and inward curling of leaves. Correction: Foliar spray of Zinc Sulphate @ 2 g/L at 30 and 45 DAT.'}. Biofertilizers: Azospirillum @ 1 kg/acre + PSB @ 1 kg/acre seedling root dip for 30 minutes..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Potato
content: Nutrient Management for Potato: RDF: 60 : 32 : 40 kg NPK/acre (150 : 80 : 100 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (DAP 70 kg) + Full Potash (MOP 67 kg or SOP Potassium Sulphate 80 kg for superior chip processing quality) + 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 50 kg) placed in furrows 5 cm away from seed tubers.. Top dressing: Remaining 1/2 Nitrogen (Urea 50 kg) top dressed at earthing up (30-35 DAP) when plants are 15-20 cm high.. Micronutrients: {'magnesium_deficiency': 'Interveinal chlorosis and necrotic brown spotting of lower leaves. Correction: Foliar spray of Magnesium Sulphate @ 5 g/L.'}. Biofertilizers: Azotobacter @ 1 kg/acre + PSB @ 1 kg/acre tuber slurry treatment..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Turmeric
content: Nutrient Management for Turmeric: RDF: 48 : 24 : 36 kg NPK/acre (120 : 60 : 90 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Full Phosphorus (SSP 150 kg) + 1/4th Nitrogen (Urea 25 kg) + 1/3rd Potash (MOP 20 kg) incorporated into beds along with 10 tonnes FYM + 200 kg neem cake.. Top dressing: Apply remaining Nitrogen and Potash in 3 equal splits at 40 DAP (1st tillering), 80 DAP (rhizome initiation), and 120 DAP (rhizome development) followed by earthing up and mulching.. Micronutrients: {'iron_zinc_deficiency': 'Chlorosis and pale yellow leaves. Correction: Foliar spray of Micronutrient mixture (Formula 4 / IISR Turmeric special) @ 5 g/L at 60 and 90 DAP.'}. Biofertilizers: IISR Bio-capsule (Trichoderma + PGPR) @ 1 capsule/100 L water rhizome dip..

title: Fertilizer Schedule: Black Gram / Urad
content: Nutrient Management for Black Gram / Urad: RDF: 8 : 16 : 8 kg NPK/acre (20 : 40 : 20 kg NPK/ha). Basal: Entire fertilizer dose applied as basal placement at sowing: DAP @ 35 kg + MOP @ 13 kg/acre.. Top dressing: Foliar spray of 2% DAP (20 g/L) or 19:19:19 (5 g/L) at flowering (30-35 DAS) and pod setting (45 DAS).. Micronutrients: {'iron_chlorosis': 'Terminal leaf yellowing. Correction: Foliar spray of 0.5% Ferrous Sulphate + 0.1% citric acid.'}. Biofertilizers: Rhizobium + PSB @ 250 g/10 kg seed inoculation..

title: Soil Profile: Deep Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols)
content: Soil Type: Deep Black Cotton Soils (Vertisols). Regions: Deccan Plateau: Telangana (Adilabad, Nizamabad, Khammam), Maharashtra (Vidarbha, Marathwada), Madhya Pradesh (Malwa, Nimar), Gujarat, Northern Karnataka.. Texture: Clay content 40-60% dominated by montmorillonite clay mineral; high swelling and shrinkage properties; forms wide deep cracks during dry season; self-ploughing; very high moisture retention capacity but poor internal drainage when wet.. pH: 7.5 - 8.5 (Mildly to moderately alkaline). Organic Carbon: Low to medium (0.35 - 0.55%); benchmark target >0.75%. Deficiencies: High in calcium and potassium; deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Zinc, and available Iron.. Reclamation/Amendments: Incorporate broad-bed and furrow (BBF) land configuration to drain excess monsoon surface water. Apply Gypsum @ 1-2 tonnes/acre if exchangeable sodium percentage (ESP) exceeds 15% (sodic phase). Deep summer chiseling once in 3 years.. Green Manure: Incorporate Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) or Sunnhemp (Crotalaria juncea) at 45 DAS (adds 8-10 tonnes green biomass/acre). Apply FYM @ 5 tonnes/acre..

title: Soil Profile: Red Sandy Loams (Alfisols / Chalkas)
content: Soil Type: Red Sandy Loams (Alfisols / Chalkas). Regions: Southern Telangana (Mahabubnagar, Nalgonda, Rangareddy), Andhra Pradesh (Rayalaseema), Tamil Nadu, Odisha, Chhota Nagpur plateau.. Texture: Formed by weathering of ancient granitic rocks; red color due to ferric oxides; light textured, sandy loam to sandy clay loam; high infiltration rate; low moisture retention capacity; prone to surface crusting after heavy rains.. pH: 6.0 - 7.2 (Slightly acidic to neutral). Organic Carbon: Very low (<0.40%). Deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, and Zinc.. Reclamation/Amendments: Break surface crusting using spike tooth harrow after rains. Apply tank silt @ 20-30 bullock cartloads (15 tonnes)/acre once in 4 years to enhance moisture retention and clay fraction. Ridge-furrow cultivation across slope.. Green Manure: Green manuring with Sunnhemp @ 15 kg seed/acre. Apply vermicompost @ 2 tonnes/acre or enriched FYM..

title: Soil Profile: Alluvial Soils (Entisols / Inceptisols)
content: Soil Type: Alluvial Soils (Entisols / Inceptisols). Regions: Indo-Gangetic Plains: Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, coastal river deltas of Krishna, Godavari, Mahanadi, and Cauvery.. Texture: Deposited by Himalayan and peninsular river systems; loamy sand to silty clay loam; deep friable structure; excellent porosity and capillary conductivity; highly responsive to irrigation and intensive multi-cropping.. pH: 6.5 - 7.8 (Neutral to mildly alkaline). Organic Carbon: Low to medium (0.40 - 0.60%). Deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Zinc, and Manganese (especially in rice-wheat rotations).. Reclamation/Amendments: Maintain balanced NPK stoichiometry (4:2:1 ratio). Laser land leveling to optimize water distribution and avoid localized waterlogging. Crop residue incorporation (Happy Seeder / Super Seeder technology).. Green Manure: Summer Green Mungbean / Dhaincha incorporation after wheat harvest. Inoculation with Trichoderma viride to accelerate stubble decomposition..

title: Soil Profile: Saline-Alkali / Sodic Soils (Usar / Kallar)
content: Soil Type: Saline-Alkali / Sodic Soils (Usar / Kallar). Regions: Indo-Gangetic canal command areas (UP, Punjab, Haryana), canal irrigated pockets of Telangana and Karnataka, coastal tracts of Gujarat and AP.. Texture: High soluble salts (EC > 4.0 dS/m in saline soils) or high exchangeable sodium (ESP > 15%, SAR > 13, pH > 8.5 in sodic/alkali soils); soil particles disperse creating impermeable slickenside; severe drainage failure; white or black encrustation.. pH: 8.5 - 10.2 (Strongly alkaline). Organic Carbon: Extremely low (<0.25%). Deficiencies: Extreme deficiency of Zinc, Iron, and available Calcium; toxic accumulation of Sodium, Carbonates, and Boron.. Reclamation/Amendments: Compute Gypsum Requirement (GR). Apply agricultural grade Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O @ 70-80% purity) @ 3-5 tonnes/acre broadcast and mixed in top 10 cm soil, followed by impounding 10-15 cm water for 15 days to leach displaced sodium down drains. Provide subsurface tile drainage.. Green Manure: Grow Dhaincha (Sesbania aculeata) tolerant to pH up to 9.5; incorporate at 45 DAS (releases carbonic acid during decomposition which neutralizes sodicity). Apply press mud @ 5 tonnes/acre..
citation: ICAR-CSSRI Karnal Reclamation of Sodic Soils Handbook 2025

title: Soil Profile: Acid Soils (Ultisols / Oxisols)
content: Soil Type: Acid Soils (Ultisols / Oxisols). Regions: High rainfall hilly zones: North-Eastern States, Kerala, Coastal Karnataka, Konkan Maharashtra, Chhota Nagpur plateau of Jharkhand and Odisha.. Texture: Intense tropical leaching removes basic cations (Ca, Mg, K, Na); dominated by kaolinite clay and iron/aluminium oxides; high phosphorus fixation capacity (P gets locked as insoluble aluminium and iron phosphates).. pH: 4.2 - 5.5 (Strongly to moderately acidic). Organic Carbon: Medium to high (0.75 - 1.2%). Deficiencies: Severe deficiency of Phosphorus, Calcium, Magnesium, Boron, and Molybdenum; Aluminium and Manganese toxicity.. Reclamation/Amendments: Liming: Apply agricultural limestone (CaCO3) or dolomite (CaCO3·MgCO3) @ 1.0 - 2.5 tonnes/acre based on soil buffer capacity once in 3 years. Apply Rock Phosphate (RP) instead of water-soluble SSP, as acid soil naturally dissolves rock phosphate.. Green Manure: Apply well-rotted FYM @ 5 tonnes/acre + biofertilizers (Phosphate Solubilizing Fungi like Aspergillus awamori)..
citation: ICAR-IISS Bhopal Acid Soil Amelioration Guide 2025

title: Soil Profile: Laterite Soils
content: Soil Type: Laterite Soils. Regions: Western Ghats, Coastal Kerala, Karnataka, Ratnagiri (Maharashtra), parts of Odisha and West Bengal.. Texture: Coarse, porous, honey-combed structure rich in iron and aluminium sesquioxides; poor nutrient holding capacity; low cation exchange capacity (CEC); rapid organic matter oxidation.. pH: 5.0 - 6.2 (Acidic). Organic Carbon: Low to medium (0.45 - 0.70%). Deficiencies: Deficient in Potassium, Calcium, Magnesium, Boron, and available Phosphorus.. Reclamation/Amendments: Split application of chemical fertilizers to avoid leaching loss. Apply Dolomite @ 500 kg/acre to replenish Calcium and Magnesium. Mulching to protect surface from heavy rainfall erosion.. Green Manure: Intercropping with velvet bean (Mucuna pruriens) or cowpea. Application of coir pith compost @ 3 tonnes/acre..

title: Soil Profile: Coastal Saline Soils
content: Soil Type: Coastal Saline Soils. Regions: Sundarbans (West Bengal), Coastal Odisha, Andhra Pradesh (Krishna-Godavari delta coastal fringe), Tamil Nadu, Gujarat (Rann of Kutch).. Texture: Periodic sea water inundation and high shallow saline groundwater table; high electrical conductivity (EC > 8.0 dS/m); heavy clay to silty loam texture with poor aeration.. pH: 6.8 - 8.2. Organic Carbon: Medium (0.50 - 0.80%). Deficiencies: High in Sodium and Chlorides; low in Nitrogen and Zinc.. Reclamation/Amendments: Construct perimeter bunds with one-way flap sluice gates to prevent tidal ingress. Raised-bed and sunken-furrow system (grow paddy in furrows and vegetables on raised beds). Leaching with fresh rainwater during monsoon.. Green Manure: Cultivate salt-tolerant halophytic green manures; incorporate organic paddy straw mulch to suppress capillary salt ascent during dry summer months..
citation: ICAR-CSSRI Regional Research Station Canning Town 2025

title: Soil Profile: Calcareous Soils
content: Soil Type: Calcareous Soils. Regions: Northern Bihar, Saurashtra (Gujarat), parts of Western Rajasthan, Rayalaseema (AP), and Belgaum (Karnataka).. Texture: Contain free calcium carbonate (CaCO3 > 5% to 20%) in form of soft powdery lime or hard nodules (kankar); high buffering capacity; causes precipitation of phosphate and micronutrients.. pH: 7.8 - 8.6 (Alkaline). Organic Carbon: Low (0.30 - 0.45%). Deficiencies: Severe fixation of Phosphorus; acute Iron deficiency (lime-induced iron chlorosis) and Zinc deficiency.. Reclamation/Amendments: Band placement of phosphatic fertilizers with acidic fertilizers like Ammonium Sulphate instead of Urea. Apply elemental sulphur @ 200 kg/acre to create localized acidic micro-zones.. Green Manure: Incorporate green manure crops; application of press mud cake (PMC) @ 5 tonnes/acre which produces organic acids upon rotting..

title: Soil Profile: Desert / Arid Sandy Soils (Aridisols)
content: Soil Type: Desert / Arid Sandy Soils (Aridisols). Regions: Western Rajasthan (Thar Desert: Jodhpur, Barmer, Bikaner, Jaisalmer), South-Western Punjab, Haryana fringe.. Texture: Coarse sand (>85% sand fraction); single-grain structure; excessive permeability; very poor water retention capacity (wilting point reached in 2-3 days); prone to severe wind erosion.. pH: 7.5 - 8.5. Organic Carbon: Extremely low (<0.20%). Deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potassium, Zinc, and Copper.. Reclamation/Amendments: Shelterbelts and windbreaks using Acacia tortilis and Prosopis cineraria (Khejri). Compaction of sandy subsoil with heavy rollers to reduce percolation loss. Drip irrigation with fertigation mandatory.. Green Manure: Incorporate Guar (Cluster bean) @ 15 kg/acre. Application of Bentonite clay @ 4 tonnes/acre in root zone to improve water holding capacity..

title: Soil Profile: Medium Black Soils (Inceptic Vertisols)
content: Soil Type: Medium Black Soils (Inceptic Vertisols). Regions: Telangana (Warangal, Karimnagar), Maharashtra (Western plains), MP (Indore, Ujjain), Karnataka (Dharwad).. Texture: Depth 50-100 cm; clay content 35-45%; dark brown to black; good balance of drainage and moisture retention compared to deep heavy vertisols; versatile for two-crop rotations (Soybean-Wheat or Cotton-Pulse).. pH: 7.2 - 8.2. Organic Carbon: Low to medium (0.45 - 0.65%). Deficiencies: Deficient in Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Sulphur, and Zinc.. Reclamation/Amendments: Contour bunding and vegetative barriers (Vetiver grass hedgerows) to arrest soil erosion. Regular addition of FYM.. Green Manure: Intercropping with Pigeonpea / Cowpea; green leaf manuring with Subabul (Leucaena leucocephala) loppings..

title: Soil Profile: Peaty and Marshy Soils (Kari Soils / Histosols)
content: Soil Type: Peaty and Marshy Soils (Kari Soils / Histosols). Regions: Kottayam and Alappuzha districts of Kerala (Kuttanad submerged tracts), coastal Odisha, Sundarbans.. Texture: Formed under anaerobic waterlogged conditions; dark black color; spongy consistency; very high accumulation of undecomposed organic matter; contains iron pyrite (FeS2) which oxidizes to sulphuric acid on drainage producing acid sulphate conditions.. pH: 3.5 - 4.5 (Extremely acidic upon drying). Organic Carbon: Very high (10 - 40%). Deficiencies: Low available Phosphorus; Potassium and Copper deficiency; Iron and Aluminium toxicity.. Reclamation/Amendments: Subsurface drainage with controlled water table management. Heavy liming using burnt quicklime (CaO) or hydrated lime @ 2-3 tonnes/acre to neutralize acidity.. Green Manure: Application of wood ash @ 1 tonne/acre to supply potash and neutralize acidity. Balanced biofertilizers..
citation: KAU Regional Agricultural Research Station Kumarakom 2025

title: Soil Profile: Sub-Montane / Hill Soils
content: Soil Type: Sub-Montane / Hill Soils. Regions: Himalayan foothills: Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Nilgiris (Tamil Nadu).. Texture: Formed under temperate forest cover; loam to sandy loam texture with stones and pebbles; high gravel content; shallow to medium depth on steep slopes.. pH: 5.5 - 6.8 (Slightly acidic). Organic Carbon: High (1.0 - 2.5% in surface horizon). Deficiencies: Deficient in Phosphorus, Zinc, and Boron.. Reclamation/Amendments: Bench terracing, contour trenching, and inward sloping terraces with vegetative grassed waterways to eliminate slope run-off erosion. Mulching with pine needles or oak leaves.. Green Manure: Incorporation of white clover (Trifolium repens) as cover crop; application of well-cured sheep manure or compost @ 5 tonnes/acre..

title: Irrigation Guide: Cotton
content: Irrigation for Cotton: Water Requirement: 700 - 1200 mm. Critical stages: Squaring Stage (Floral bud formation) (45 - 55 DAS): Water stress leads to massive square shedding.; Peak Flowering (65 - 80 DAS): Critical for flower retention and pollen viability.; Boll Development Stage (90 - 120 DAS): Severe stress causes young boll drop and shorter fiber staple length.. Methods: {'drip_irrigation': 'Inline drip system with 16 mm lateral per crop row, 40-50 cm dripper spacing, 2.0 - 4.0 LPH discharge rate. Operates 2-3 hours every alternate day. Achieves 40-50% water savings and allows fertigation.', 'furrow_irrigation': 'Alternate furrow irrigation method saves 30-35% water without reducing yield. Irrigate when soil moisture depletes to 50% available water capacity.'}. Water stress management: If moisture stress occurs during dry spells, give foliar spray of 2% Potassium Nitrate (KNO3 @ 20 g/L) or 1% Urea to reduce leaf senescence and square drop..

title: Irrigation Guide: Rice / Paddy
content: Irrigation for Rice / Paddy: Water Requirement: 1100 - 1500 mm. Critical stages: Seedling Establishment / Initial Tillering (1 - 10 DAT): Requires 2 cm standing water for root anchor.; Panicle Initiation (PI) (45 - 55 DAT): Water deficit drastically reduces spikelet number per panicle.; Booting to Heading (65 - 80 DAT): Extreme sensitivity; drought causes spikelet sterility and chaffy ears.; Flowering / Anthesis (80 - 90 DAT): Requires saturated soil; stress causes floret abortion.; Milk Stage (90 - 105 DAT): Grain filling requires adequate moisture.. Methods: {'alternate_wetting_and_drying_awd': 'Install perforated field water tube (Pani Pipe) of 30 cm length. Re-irrigate to 5 cm depth only when water level inside tube drops to 15 cm below soil surface. Saves 25-30% irrigation water and reduces methane emissions.', 'continuous_flooding': 'Maintain 2-5 cm shallow standing water during critical reproductive stages.'}. Water stress management: Drain standing water completely 10-12 days before anticipated harvest to facilitate uniform grain drying and mechanical combine movement..

title: Irrigation Guide: Chilli
content: Irrigation for Chilli: Water Requirement: 600 - 900 mm. Critical stages: Establishment after Transplanting (1 - 10 DAT): Light frequent irrigations prevent seedling mortality.; Flower Initiation (35 - 50 DAT): Moisture stress causes flower bud drop.; Fruit Set & Early Berry Development (60 - 90 DAT): Deficit causes fruit drop and small distorted pods.. Methods: {'drip_irrigation': 'Paired row planting with 16 mm lateral between two rows; 30 cm dripper spacing with 2 LPH drippers; run 1.5 - 2.5 hours every alternate day.', 'ridge_furrow': 'Irrigate furrow up to 2/3rd height of ridge to avoid water wetting root crown directly (prevents collar rot).'}. Water stress management: Avoid water stagnation at all costs; stagnant water for >12 hours triggers immediate root asphyxiation and wilting..

title: Irrigation Guide: Tomato
content: Irrigation for Tomato: Water Requirement: 400 - 600 mm. Critical stages: Early Vegetative Growth (15 - 30 DAT): Moderate moisture promotes deep root architecture.; Flowering & Fruit Set (35 - 55 DAT): Stress leads to flower drop and poor blossom fertilization.; Fruit Enlargement / Bulking (55 - 80 DAT): Irregular watering induces blossom end rot and radial fruit cracking.. Methods: {'drip_irrigation_with_mulch': 'Drip system with silver-black polyethylene mulch (30 micron) reduces crop water demand by 45% and eliminates weed competition.', 'furrow_irrigation': 'Irrigate every 5-7 days in summer, 8-10 days in winter.'}. Water stress management: Maintain steady, uniform soil moisture; heavy irrigation after a dry spell is the primary cause of fruit skin cracking..

title: Irrigation Guide: Wheat
content: Irrigation for Wheat: Water Requirement: 450 - 650 mm. Critical stages: Crown Root Initiation (CRI) (20 - 25 DAS): Most critical irrigation stage in wheat; delay causes 35-40% irreversible yield penalty.; Tillering Stage (40 - 45 DAS): Governs effective ear-bearing tiller number.; Late Jointing Stage (60 - 65 DAS): Determines floret number per spikelet.; Flowering / Anthesis (80 - 85 DAS): Pollination and fertilization phase.; Milk Stage (95 - 100 DAS): Affects initial grain filling rate.; Dough Stage (105 - 115 DAS): Ensures grain test weight and prevents shriveling.. Methods: {'border_strip_irrigation': 'Check basin or border strip (6m x 40m) designed for uniform water spread; apply 60-70 mm depth per irrigation.', 'sprinkler_irrigation': 'Suitable for undulated topography and light sandy soils; saves 30% water and protects against frost.'}. Water stress management: If only 1 irrigation available: Apply at CRI (21 DAS). If 2 irrigations: Apply at CRI and Flowering. If 3: CRI, Late Jointing, and Milk stage..

title: Irrigation Guide: Maize
content: Irrigation for Maize: Water Requirement: 500 - 800 mm. Critical stages: Knee-High Stage (V6-V8) (30 - 35 DAS): Rapid vegetative growth and ear shoot initiation.; Tasseling (VT) (50 - 55 DAS): Extreme sensitivity; water stress delays silking relative to pollen shed (ASI - Anthesis Silking Interval expands) causing bare cobs.; Silking (R1) (55 - 65 DAS): Desiccation of silks leads to poor fertilization.; Early Grain Filling / Dough Stage (75 - 85 DAS): Kernel depth and test weight development.. Methods: {'furrow_irrigation': 'Irrigate in furrows with plants grown on ridges; avoids direct waterlogging of collar roots.', 'drip_irrigation': 'Inline drip lateral spaced at 60 cm row spacing with fertigation.'}. Water stress management: Maize cannot tolerate water stagnation for more than 24 hours at knee-high stage; provide instant field drainage channels..

title: Irrigation Guide: Groundnut / Peanut
content: Irrigation for Groundnut / Peanut: Water Requirement: 500 - 700 mm. Critical stages: Flowering Stage (25 - 35 DAS): Ensures maximum flower production.; Peg Penetration (Pegging) (35 - 50 DAS): Upper 5 cm soil must remain moist and friable to permit peg penetration without mechanical resistance.; Pod Development Stage (55 - 75 DAS): Kernel enlargement; moisture stress causes 'pops' (empty pods).. Methods: {'sprinkler_irrigation': 'Sprinkler system operated in morning or late evening; highly effective for softening soil surface during peg entry.', 'broad_bed_and_furrow': 'BBF method (beds 120 cm wide, furrows 30 cm) with irrigation through furrows.'}. Water stress management: Withhold irrigation during early vegetative phase (10-25 DAS) to encourage deeper taproot elongation; resume at flowering..

title: Irrigation Guide: Soybean
content: Irrigation for Soybean: Water Requirement: 550 - 750 mm. Critical stages: Flowering (R1-R2) (35 - 45 DAS): Moisture deficit causes flower abortion and poor pod set.; Pod Filling (R4-R5) (55 - 75 DAS): Affects seed size, oil concentration, and seed shriveling.. Methods: {'broad_bed_furrow_bbf': 'BBF system facilitates drainage during heavy monsoon cloudbursts and serves as irrigation furrows during dry spells.', 'sprinkler_irrigation': 'Supplemental sprinkler irrigation during mid-season monsoon dry spells.'}. Water stress management: If rainfed dry spell exceeds 15 days during pod fill, give 1 protective irrigation of 50 mm..

title: Irrigation Guide: Red Gram / Pigeonpea
content: Irrigation for Red Gram / Pigeonpea: Water Requirement: 600 - 800 mm. Critical stages: Flower Bud Initiation (75 - 85 DAS): Prevents floral drop during post-monsoon dry spell.; Pod Setting and Development (100 - 120 DAS): Critical for bold seed development.. Methods: {'protective_irrigation': '1-2 protective furrow irrigations during terminal drought in October-November increase grain yield by 35-50%.'}. Water stress management: Foliar spray of 2% Urea or 1% KNO3 during dry spells reduces drought-induced shedding..

title: Irrigation Guide: Chickpea / Bengal Gram
content: Irrigation for Chickpea / Bengal Gram: Water Requirement: 250 - 400 mm. Critical stages: Pre-flowering / Late Vegetative (40 - 45 DAS): Branching and floral bud development.; Pod Initiation (65 - 75 DAS): Directly impacts seed weight.. Methods: {'light_furrow_irrigation': 'Apply light irrigation (50-60 mm). Never flood chickpea fields, as excess moisture triggers Fusarium wilt and collar rot.', 'sprinkler_irrigation': '1-2 light sprinkler rounds.'}. Water stress management: DO NOT irrigate chickpea during active flowering (50-60 DAS) as it triggers excessive vegetative growth and flower drop..

title: Irrigation Guide: Mustard / Rapeseed
content: Irrigation for Mustard / Rapeseed: Water Requirement: 300 - 450 mm. Critical stages: Rosette to Pre-flowering (30 - 35 DAS): Promotes secondary branching and siliquae points.; Pod (Siliqua) Filling (60 - 70 DAS): Ensures full seed formation and oil synthesis.. Methods: {'check_basin_irrigation': 'Apply 60 mm irrigation per round.', 'sprinkler_irrigation': 'Highly effective on undulating semi-arid topography.'}. Water stress management: Ensure 1st irrigation is given without fail at 30-35 DAS after completing thinning and weeding..

title: Irrigation Guide: Sugarcane
content: Irrigation for Sugarcane: Water Requirement: 1500 - 2500 mm. Critical stages: Sprouting / Germination (1 - 35 DAP): Requires moist soil for bud bursting.; Tillering (Formative Stage) (35 - 120 DAP): Determines millable cane population per acre.; Grand Growth Stage (120 - 270 DAP): Maximum daily water consumption; water stress shortens internodes.. Methods: {'subsurface_or_surface_drip': 'Drip irrigation with 1.5 - 2.5 LPH drippers saves 50% irrigation water and increases cane yield by 25-35%.', 'alternate_furrow': 'Trash mulching in alternate furrows saves 30% water.'}. Water stress management: Withhold irrigation 15-20 days before harvest to promote sucrose accumulation and higher brix sugar recovery..

title: Irrigation Guide: Onion
content: Irrigation for Onion: Water Requirement: 350 - 550 mm. Critical stages: Establishment (1 - 10 DAT): Light watering for seedling root catch.; Bulb Initiation (50 - 65 DAT): Cell division in bulb scales.; Bulb Development & Bulking (65 - 95 DAT): High water demand; stress causes splitting and double bulbs.. Methods: {'micro_sprinkler_or_drip': 'Micro-sprinklers provide uniform moisture distribution and lower canopy temperature during hot dry periods.', 'flat_bed_irrigation': 'Irrigate every 5-6 days in summer and 8-10 days in winter.'}. Water stress management: Stop irrigation 10-15 days before harvesting when 50% top neck-fall occurs to cure outer bulb scales and prevent storage rot..

title: Irrigation Guide: Potato
content: Irrigation for Potato: Water Requirement: 450 - 600 mm. Critical stages: Stolon Formation & Tuber Initiation (25 - 40 DAP): Determines number of tubers set per hill.; Tuber Bulking Stage (45 - 75 DAP): Rapid starch deposition; water stress causes hollow heart, cracked or misshapen tubers.. Methods: {'furrow_irrigation': 'Maintain water level up to 2/3rd height of ridges; never allow water to submerge ridge tops.', 'sprinkler_irrigation': 'Uniform wetting in sandy loam tracts.'}. Water stress management: Stop irrigation 10-12 days before dehaulming/harvest to allow tuber skin to harden..

title: Irrigation Guide: Turmeric
content: Irrigation for Turmeric: Water Requirement: 1200 - 1800 mm. Critical stages: Rhizome Sprouting (1 - 30 DAP): Requires moist environment under green leaf mulch.; Tillering & Early Bulking (60 - 120 DAP): Vegetative canopy development.; Rhizome Development & Finger Expansion (120 - 180 DAP): Maximum biomass accumulation.. Methods: {'drip_irrigation_on_beds': 'Paired lateral on 120 cm raised beds saves 35-40% water and prevents rhizome rot water stagnation.', 'ridge_and_furrow': 'Frequent light irrigations at 7-10 day intervals.'}. Water stress management: Provide instant drainage during monsoon downpours; standing water triggers soft rot (Pythium) epidemic..

title: Irrigation Guide: Black Gram / Urad
content: Irrigation for Black Gram / Urad: Water Requirement: 350 - 500 mm. Critical stages: Flowering Stage (25 - 35 DAS): Essential for flower retention.; Pod Filling (40 - 55 DAS): Crucial for seed sizing.. Methods: {'border_or_furrow': '1-2 light irrigations under irrigated situations; for rice-fallow relay crop, depends on residual moisture.'}. Water stress management: Foliar spray of 2% DAP at flowering boosts pod set under receding soil moisture..

title: Cropping System: Cotton + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Cotton + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 4:1, 6:1 or 8:1 (4-8 rows of Cotton followed by 1 row of Pigeonpea). Zones: Telangana, Vidarbha (Maharashtra), Northern Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh black soil drylands.. Synergies: Pigeonpea is a deep-rooted legume that accesses subsoil moisture from different soil horizons than cotton. Fixes 40-60 kg atmospheric Nitrogen/ha, improves soil aggregation, and acts as an insurance crop against bollworm crop failure.. LER: LER: 1.35 - 1.45 (35-45% greater biological productivity than monocultures). Pest benefits: Pigeonpea serves as a barrier and refuge crop for bollworm parasitoids (Campoletis chloridae and Trichogramma)..

title: Cropping System: Groundnut + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Groundnut + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 7:1 or 8:1 (7-8 rows of Groundnut to 1 row of Pigeonpea). Zones: Rayalaseema (AP), Southern Telangana (Mahabubnagar), Saurashtra (Gujarat), Karnataka alfisols.. Synergies: Complementary canopy architecture: Groundnut forms dense horizontal ground cover suppressing weeds and conserving moisture, while Pigeonpea produces tall vertical canopy. Both are legumes contributing biological nitrogen fixation.. LER: LER: 1.28 - 1.38. Pest benefits: Reduces incidence of groundnut leaf miner and tikka leaf spot..

title: Cropping System: Soybean + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Soybean + Pigeonpea (Red Gram) Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 4:2 (4 rows of Soybean and 2 rows of Pigeonpea). Zones: Madhya Pradesh (Malwa, Nimar, Central Vindhyas), Maharashtra (Vidarbha, Marathwada).. Synergies: Temporal complementarity: Soybean matures in 90-95 days and is harvested, after which Pigeonpea expands into the vacated space during October-December using residual subsoil moisture.. LER: LER: 1.40 - 1.52. Pest benefits: Deters Spodoptera litura armyworm outbreaks..

title: Cropping System: Rice - Chickpea / Bengal Gram Relay Cropping (Paira / Utera)
content: Cropping System: Rice - Chickpea / Bengal Gram Relay Cropping (Paira / Utera). Spacing/Ratio: Sequential relay broadcasting: Chickpea seeds broadcast into standing paddy 2-3 days before harvest. Zones: Eastern UP, Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal rice fallows.. Synergies: Utilizes residual soil moisture and capillary water after Kharif rice without tillage; legume root nodules enrich soil nitrogen (30-40 kg N/ha) for succeeding Kharif crops; eliminates fallow land degradation.. LER: Cropping Intensity increased from 100% to 200%. Pest benefits: Breaks cycle of rice monophagous pests like Yellow Stem Borer and Brown Plant Hopper..

title: Cropping System: Maize + Black Gram / Green Gram Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Maize + Black Gram / Green Gram Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 1:2 or 2:2 additive series. Zones: Telangana, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Bihar.. Synergies: Maize utilizes high light and nitrogen, while pulses cover inter-row space rapidly suppressing weeds and fixing 30 kg N/acre. Pulse harvest at 65-70 days provides early cash flow.. LER: LER: 1.25 - 1.35. Pest benefits: Reduces maize stem borer egg laying on primary host..

title: Cropping System: Sugarcane + Cowpea / French Bean Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Sugarcane + Cowpea / French Bean Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 1:2 (2 rows of pulse in 120 cm or 150 cm wide sugarcane inter-row spaces). Zones: Western Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Telangana canal command areas.. Synergies: Sugarcane has slow early formative growth (up to 90 days); short-duration pulses (55-65 days) mature before cane canopy closes, producing 4-6 quintals of pulse grain per acre without reducing cane yields.. LER: LER: 1.30 - 1.40. Pest benefits: Suppresses early weed growth and provides live mulch conserving furrow moisture..

title: Cropping System: Rice - Wheat - Green Gram (Summer Mung) Triple Cropping
content: Cropping System: Rice - Wheat - Green Gram (Summer Mung) Triple Cropping. Spacing/Ratio: 300% Sequential Cropping Rotation: Kharif Rice -> Rabi Wheat -> Summer Mungbean (60 days). Zones: Punjab, Haryana, Western Uttar Pradesh Indo-Gangetic Plains.. Synergies: Incorporating short-duration summer green gram (SML 668 / Virat) in April-June fixes 40-50 kg N/ha, adds 3 tonnes green biomass/acre upon threshing, and rejuvenates exhausted rice-wheat soil organic carbon.. LER: Cropping Intensity: 300%; saves 25% fertilizer N in succeeding paddy. Pest benefits: Reduces Phalaris minor seed bank through summer solarization and tillage..

title: Cropping System: Sorghum + Pigeonpea Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Sorghum + Pigeonpea Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 2:1 (2 rows Sorghum : 1 row Pigeonpea). Zones: Semi-Arid Tropics: Deccan Plateau, Karnataka, Maharashtra drylands.. Synergies: Proven risk-aversion cropping system for drought-prone drylands; Sorghum harvested at 100 days; Pigeonpea continues to grow until 160 days on deep vertisol moisture.. LER: LER: 1.38 - 1.48. Pest benefits: Minimizes Striga weed emergence and builds predatory insect populations..

title: Cropping System: Mustard + Chickpea Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Mustard + Chickpea Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 4:1 or 6:1 (4-6 rows Chickpea : 1 row Mustard). Zones: Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana, Bundelkhand.. Synergies: Mustard tall stature acts as windbreak; roots explore different soil layers; Chickpea fixes atmospheric nitrogen; mustard acts as trap crop for pod borer predators.. LER: LER: 1.20 - 1.30. Pest benefits: Mustard glucosinolate root exudates suppress soil-borne fungal pathogens..

title: Cropping System: Cotton - Groundnut Biennial Rotation
content: Cropping System: Cotton - Groundnut Biennial Rotation. Spacing/Ratio: Crop rotation: Kharif Cotton -> Summer Green Manure -> Kharif Groundnut -> Rabi Bengal Gram. Zones: Saurashtra (Gujarat), Northern Telangana, Western Maharashtra.. Synergies: Breaks monoculture build-up of Pink Bollworm in soil; groundnut fixes nitrogen, lowering fertilizer cost for succeeding cotton by 25%.. LER: Improves soil health index by 28%. Pest benefits: Disrupts life cycle of soil-pupating bollworms..

title: Cropping System: Turmeric + Maize / Chilli Border Intercropping
content: Cropping System: Turmeric + Maize / Chilli Border Intercropping. Spacing/Ratio: 1 row of Maize after every 10 rows of Turmeric; or Castor on borders. Zones: Telangana (Nizamabad, Jagtial), Andhra Pradesh (Duggirala), Tamil Nadu (Erode).. Synergies: Maize provides partial shade to turmeric during early scorching summer months (May-June) when young sprouts emerge, reducing sunburn; maize cobs harvested at 85 days.. LER: LER: 1.25 - 1.35. Pest benefits: Reduces shoot borer immigration into turmeric canopy..

title: Cropping System: Dhaincha Green Manure - Rice - Rabi Pulse Rotation
content: Cropping System: Dhaincha Green Manure - Rice - Rabi Pulse Rotation. Spacing/Ratio: Sequential rotation: Summer Dhaincha (45 days) -> Kharif Rice -> Rabi Urad / Mung. Zones: Godavari Delta, Krishna Delta, Cauvery Basin, Punjab, Bengal.. Synergies: Dhaincha incorporated at 45 DAS adds 8-10 tonnes organic biomass and 60-80 kg N/ha in organic form, lowering chemical nitrogen requirement by 25-50% while improving soil microbial diversity.. LER: Sustainable Yield Index (SYI) increases from 0.62 to 0.88. Pest benefits: Reduces incidence of sheath blight and nematodes..
